“I just want transparency,” said Melway’s younger brother, who FrontPage Africa/New Narratives is identifying only as M. to protect him from retaliation.

Anti-trafficking advocates have also called on the government to act.

“With that kind of gravity where somebody died, I don’t think the case can die, because if it dies, it puts the government in a very bad situation because that means they are compromising justice,” said Adolphus Satiah, head of the anti-human trafficking secretariat at the Ministry of Labor during the Weah administration. “When somebody dies, it’s not an easy case for anybody to play with, not even the government people.”

Melway’s death did not appear on the charge sheet against the 12 original defendants in the case drawn up by Enoch Dunbar, the head of the Anti-Human Trafficking Unit at the Liberia National Police, in October 2025.

That charge sheet – which had substantially downgraded most of the charges and dropped them against three of the defendants – was revised in April by Sumo C. Kutu Akoi, the senior human trafficking prosecutor. This came after FrontPage Africa/New Narratives revealed allegations by numerous victims that Bestman Juah, now head of public defenders, had offered a bribe on behalf of the traffickers to a prosecutor to downgrade the charges.

Victims allege Dunbar accepted a bribe to downgrade the charges. The case drew international attention and became a national test of Liberia’s willingness to prosecute organized trafficking networks. Previously the state had secured just six human trafficking convictions since 2020 and was on the US State Department’s Trafficking in Persons watchlist, risking aid cuts. When the charges were reinstated and the case went to trial there was still no charge related to Melway’s death even though numerous victims had detailed it in their statements to police.

The traffickers convicted in Liberia’s largest human trafficking case head into the sheriff’s room shortly after being sentenced.

At the start of the trial, Akoi told FrontPage Africa/New Narratives that the prosecution had opened an investigation into Melway’s death. He has not responded to questions about the investigation since.

Two family members of Melway—her younger brother and nephew who were also recruited from Nimba by the trafficking ring – said Melway was healthy when she was recruited in early 2025.

“She was not sick. She was well moving,” said M. speaking in Liberian English. “She was hustling on own her. She had her home.”

The jury found the traffickers forced victims to make repeated recruitment calls to family and friends lying that they were in Canada. M. said traffickers forced Melway to recruit him, and he in turn was pressured to recruit their younger sister. Melway resisted. Victims who failed to recruit new members were routinely punished. M. said food was withheld from his sister because she would not recruit more people.

“When I get there, she was not eating,” said M. “From morning all the way up to the evening, you will not eat because they will still press her to call somebody.”

The compound where Ophelia Melway and other victims were held in captivity. She fell ill there before her traffickers released her to her family for treatment shortly before she died. Credit: Anthony Stephens/New Narratives.

Melway’s deteriorating condition and death came up repeatedly during the trial, with nearly every victim mentioning it in their testimony. But still it was not proposed as a charge. Akoi did not answer questions as to why.

Another survivor, L., testified that Melway became progressively weaker, and traffickers ignored repeated warnings that Melway’s condition was worsening.

“She was sitting down the whole day, tired,” said L. “In the night when the people finished packing their chairs, we used to [sit] on the cool ground. She used to tell them she not well, but they never believe her.”

L. said that as Melway’s appearance changed dramatically, she was subjected to the same punishments as the other victims, including being forced to hold rocks in her outstretched hands, do squats until she collapsed and drink dirty water.

Although he did not testify during the trial, Melway’s nephew, identified as A., said in an interview that he watched helplessly as traffickers tried to force his aunt to continue recruiting others despite her deteriorating condition.

“I was feeling discouraged because seeing your family member in that kind of condition, I felt bad,” A. said. After learning of her death, he said he begged to leave.

“The people said, ‘No way. When they put me out, I was going to expose their secret.’”

Another relative of Melway, who testified during the trial and whom FrontPage Africa/New Narratives is identifying only as J., said Daniel Davis, one of the convicted traffickers, told victims he had given Melway US$20 to travel home to Nimba County for treatment. J. said Davis’ girlfriend, Shelly Suah, another convicted trafficker, later told them, “Oh, Ophelia na make it.”

A male victim identified only as M. testified that “she was killed.” He said Melway became seriously ill before traffickers removed her from the compound for medical treatment.

Z. said Melway was sent to the family who later took her to Ganta United Methodist Hospital.

One of the rooms of the compound.

There doctors diagnosed her with dangerously high blood pressure M. said. After three days she died.

Her death, on top of the thousands the family gave to the traffickers, had dealt a devastating blow to the family. M. said Melway was the primary provider for the family, selling rice to support her parents and paying his school fees. Melway also left behind her partner, and their 17-year-old daughter.

“I was going to school. But since she passed away, I don’t have different sponsor,” said M. “That thing, it’s paining me. Because when I think about the things that we did to do together, when I am jammed, the things she was doing, the sad moment will come over me. I am feeling discouraged.”

When news of Melway’s death reached the compound, victims testified, it sparked desperation and fear. Victims believed she had been killed and feared that the traffickers planned to kill them one by one. The victims made loud banging and screaming noises and drew the attention of security guards at the neighboring home of Vice President Jeremiah Koung who freed them. From there the victims made their way to the Paynesville magistrates’ court where they reported the crimes.

Inside the compound where Melway and other victims were held in captivity. Credit: Anthony Stephens/New Narratives.

Under Liberian law, the Ministry of Justice, which supervises the police, has the authority to initiate criminal investigations without the police. Police and prosecutors will determine whether the evidence supports charges of murder, negligent homicide or manslaughter.

Experts said the Melway case was another test of the government’s willingness to hold traffickers to account. Liberia has remained on the U.S. State Department’s trafficking watch list for two consecutive years and risks cuts to aid if it remains there again on this year’s report which is due to be released any day.

Zokerseh B. Saye, executive director of the Liberia Anti-Trafficking Scam and Victim Support Initiative, which helps expose human trafficking and scam operations and reports perpetrators to the government, said investigators should build on the evidence already presented during the trial.

“It’s clear and it’s because of the act that caused that woman to die,” he said. “We want the government to be fast with the result that the people can see the impact of human trafficking.”

This story was a collaboration with New Narratives as part of the Investigating Liberia project. Funding was provided by the Swedish International Cooperation Development Agency. The funder had no say in the story’s content.

World.title: Liberia: Ex-VP Jewel Howard Taylor’s Drug Case Delayed as Defense Seeks Medical Records, Cardiologist
World.content:
MONROVIA — The preliminary hearing in the government’s drug trafficking and money laundering case against former Vice President Jewel Howard Taylor has been delayed as her defense team seeks access to her medical records and an independent medical evaluation before she returns to court.

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh

The Monrovia City Court has reassigned the preliminary examination for Friday, September 4, 2026, at 10:00 a.m., according to a notice of assignment issued by Stipendiary Magistrate L. Ben Barco.

Taylor’s lawyers had initially asked the court to continue Tuesday’s proceedings to Wednesday, September 2, at a time convenient to the court, citing their client’s ongoing health condition.

The request was filed at approximately 7:54 a.m. on September 1, according to a handwritten notation on the document.

In their communication to the court, Taylor’s lawyers said she remains unwell but is willing to participate in all stages of the preliminary examination.

They said Taylor had a medical consultation scheduled for September 1 and had requested permission from the Ministry of Justice to be examined by a physician familiar with her medical history.

The lawyers argued that a brief postponement would allow the former vice president to receive necessary medical attention before returning to court.

The communication was signed by Cllr. Laveli Supuwood, Cllr. Kabineh Ja’neh, and Cllr. Finley Y. Karngar.

Defense Seeks Medical Records, Cardiologist

FrontPage Africa has gathered that Taylor’s defense team is also seeking a continuance to allow her lawyers to obtain her medical records and arrange for an independent doctor to assess her condition.

A source told FPA that Dr. Gomez of GIMS Medical Center requested Taylor’s medical records based on a notarized authorization signed by the former vice president.

The source said efforts were also underway to have a cardiologist examine Taylor as her defense team seeks a clearer assessment of her condition before she faces further proceedings.

Taylor was previously taken to GIMS Medical Center while in police custody after reportedly experiencing an unstable medical condition, including elevated blood pressure.

She was later returned to custody at the Monrovia Central Prison, where she remains detained.

Facing Serious Drug Charges

Taylor’s detention followed her arrest in connection with the government’s investigation into a massive cocaine seizure in the VOA community in Paynesville.

Authorities have valued the seized cocaine at more than US$317 million, making it one of the largest narcotics seizures in Liberia’s history.

The case has drawn significant public and political attention because of Taylor’s status as a former vice president and the identities of others named in the investigation.

The latest notice of assignment lists Taylor alongside Teras Zadereiko, alias Tony; Mitovil Vrovac, alias Michael; Nikola Ivancic, alias Sheikh; and others to be identified.

The charges listed include importation of controlled drugs, unlicensed exportation of controlled drugs and substances, abuse of office, illicit trafficking, criminal conspiracy, criminal facilitation, criminal solicitation, and money laundering.

The Government of Liberia, through the Ministry of Justice, is listed as the plaintiff.

The matter is before Magistrate Barco at the Monrovia City Court at the Temple of Justice.

Taylor Denies Allegations

Taylor has denied the allegations against her, while her lawyers have continued to challenge aspects of the government’s handling of the case.

Her arrest and detention have also triggered political controversy, with supporters and opposition voices questioning the circumstances surrounding the case.

The government’s prosecution stems from the broader investigation into the cocaine shipment seized in Paynesville, which authorities say was linked to an international narcotics trafficking operation.

Health Now Central to Proceedings

Taylor’s medical condition has emerged as the latest hurdle in the case.

With the defense seeking her medical records and an independent evaluation by a doctor, including a possible cardiology assessment, the question of whether she is medically fit to participate in court proceedings is now likely to feature prominently when the case returns on September 4.

For now, the former vice president remains in custody as her lawyers work to establish the full state of her health before the preliminary examination proceeds.

World.title: Liberia: GAC Clears Liberia’s 2025 Accounts, Flags US$76.9M Year-End Cash Balance
World.content:
Monrovia – Auditor General P. Garswa Jackson has released the General Auditing Commission’s (GAC) audit of the Government of Liberia’s Consolidated Fund Account for the 2025 fiscal year, giving the government’s financial statements an unqualified opinion while urging lawmakers to urgently act on recommendations contained in the report.

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh, [email protected]

The audit, covering the period January 1 to December 31, 2025, examined the government’s statement of cash receipts and payments, comparison of budgeted and actual amounts, and accompanying financial notes.

In his report dated August 2026, Auditor General Jackson said the financial statements “present fairly, in all material respects” the government’s receipts and payments as of December 31, 2025, and conform with the 2017 International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) Cash Basis of Accounting.

The audit was conducted in accordance with the International Standards of Supreme Audit Institutions (ISSAIs) and Section 2.1.3 of the General Auditing Commission Act of 2014.

GAC Urges Legislature to Act

Despite issuing a favorable audit opinion, Jackson warned that matters raised during the audit require the attention of the Legislature.

In a transmittal letter addressed to the Speaker of the House of Representatives and the President Pro-Tempore of the Liberian Senate, the Auditor General said the findings had been formally communicated to the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning through a Management Letter.

He said responses provided by the Ministry were reviewed and incorporated into the final audit report.

“Given the significance of the matters raised in this report,” Jackson urged lawmakers to consider implementing the audit recommendations with urgency.

The report now places responsibility on the Legislature to scrutinize the findings and follow up on the government’s implementation of the recommendations.

Government Managed US$955.2M in Cash Receipts

According to the financial statements, the government recorded US$955.20 million in total cash receipts during fiscal year 2025, a substantial increase from the US$685.56 million recorded in 2024.

The increase of approximately US$269.64 million, or 28 percent, was attributed largely to improvements in revenue administration, digital transformation and enhanced revenue collection and compliance.

The government said the integration of the Liberia Tax Administration System (LITAS) with commercial banks and mobile money platforms, along with the expansion of ASYCUDA and LITAS across major customs and tax offices, contributed to the improved performance.

Total cash expenditure also increased significantly, reaching US$902.77 million, compared with US$660.57 million in 2024.

That represents an increase of approximately US$242.20 million, or 27 percent.

The government attributed the increase partly to the settlement of outstanding commitments from the previous fiscal year’s 90-day window period and adjustments to budgeted expenditure.

US$76.89M Remained at Year-End

The financial statements show that Liberia closed fiscal year 2025 with a reconciled cash balance of approximately US$76.89 million.

The reported balance comprised funds held across government accounts, including consolidated accounts, escrow accounts, the Road Fund escrow accounts, mobile money accounts, and transitory and other accounts.

The report lists approximately:

US$14.37 million in Consolidated Accounts;

US$7.04 million in Other Escrow Accounts;

US$902,000 in Road Fund Escrow Accounts;

US$53,000 in Mobile Money Accounts;

US$58 million in Transitory and Other Accounts; and

approximately US$3.48 million in foreign currency gain/loss adjustments.

The government stated that the reconciled balances were controlled by the government and held at the Central Bank of Liberia, commercial banks and electronic platforms.

Revenue Outperformed Budget

The audit report also highlights stronger-than-projected revenue performance during the year.

The government had approved a US$880.66 million resource envelope for fiscal year 2025, representing a 19.2 percent increase over the FY2024 recast budget of US$738.86 million.

Actual overall revenue reached US$885.10 million, exceeding the approved budget by approximately US$4.44 million, or 0.5 percent.

Domestic revenue was particularly strong, reaching US$847.05 million against a budget projection of US$804.63 million—an overperformance of approximately US$42.43 million.

However, the government fell short of its projected external revenue after approximately US$40 million expected from the World Bank was not realized during FY2025 because of unmet disbursement conditions.

US$880.66M Expenditure Envelope

The FY2025 budget authorized total expenditure of US$880.66 million.

Of that amount, recurrent and non-PSIP capital expenditure accounted for US$773.95 million, or 87.9 percent, while the Public Sector Investment Program (PSIP) accounted for US$106.72 million, or 12.1 percent.

Actual cash spending, however, reached US$902.77 million, exceeding the approved expenditure envelope.

The government said the higher expenditure was influenced by the payment of outstanding commitments carried over from the previous fiscal year’s 90-day window and upward adjustments to expenditure during the reporting period.

Government Claims Stronger Financial Controls

In its statement of responsibility, the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning maintained that the government had upheld its obligations under the Public Financial Management Act and Regulations.

The government said it had systems of internal control and risk management designed to safeguard public resources against loss, misuse and fraud, ensure transactions comply with applicable laws and regulations, and maintain reliable financial records.

The Comptroller and Accountant General also certified responsibility for the accuracy, completeness and reliability of the financial information contained in the consolidated financial statements.

The financial statements were approved for issuance on April 30, 2026, while the Auditor General’s report was issued in August 2026.

Audit Opinion Does Not Mean No Problems

While the Auditor General’s unqualified opinion represents a positive assessment of the financial statements, the report makes clear that an audit opinion is not a guarantee that every instance of fraud, error or internal-control weakness will be detected.

Jackson noted that an audit provides reasonable assurance, rather than absolute assurance, that financial statements are free from material misstatement.

The Auditor General said the audit procedures were designed based on assessed risks of material misstatement, including those arising from fraud or error, and included an evaluation of accounting policies, estimates and the overall presentation of the financial statements.

The release of the report comes amid heightened public scrutiny of government spending, revenue collection and financial accountability, making the Legislature’s promised consideration of the GAC’s recommendations a key next step in determining whether the identified issues will result in corrective action.

World.title: CAF CUP: Malagasy side plots Arrows fall
World.content:
Madagascar’s FC Rouge have arrived in Zambia ahead of their CAF Confederation Cup first round preliminary first leg against Red Arrows FC set for this Saturday at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium.

‎

‎A 42-member delegation, comprising a 23-man playing squad plus technical staff and club officials, touched down at Simon Mwansa Kapwepwe International Airport on Wednesday at 15:45 hours aboard an ET flight via Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

‎

‎The visitors were received by officials from the Football Association of Zambia (FAZ) and Red Arrows FC.

‎

‎Speaking upon arrival, FC Rouge head coach Fenososa Maldini said the team was ready for the continental battle and impressed with the reception in Ndola.

‎

‎“We are happy with the way we have been received. From what we have seen so far, we believe our stay here will be good,”_ Maldini said.

‎

‎The Malagasy tactician admitted preparations were tough but said his side did its homework.

‎

‎“We did prepare very well although it is always difficult we will try to persevere,” he said.

‎

‎“We only tried to find out more about Red Arrows through social media. We did our homework and we are here with an ambition to get a positive result. Our objective is to win the first round,” Maldini added.

‎

‎The FC Rouge delegation has checked into Kwetu Lodge in the Dola Hill area of Ndola where they will base and finalize preparations ahead of the match.

‎

‎The encounter on Saturday, 5 September 2026 at 15:00 hours at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium carries significant continental stakes, with both sides seeking a first-leg advantage ahead of the return fixture in Madagascar.

‎

‎Red Arrows will be banking on home support as they kick off their African campaign, with anticipation building for what promises to be a fiercely contested CAF Confederation Cup tie.

World.title: Nalolo leaders commend President’s call for unity
World.content:
Nalolo District Commissioner Namatama Mupo has described President Hakainde Hichilema’s inauguration speech as a call for unity, hard work and service delivery for all Zambians.

Reacting to the President’s address, Ms Mupo said the Head of State has continued to champion the One Zambia, One Nation motto by urging citizens to reject tribalism, violence and hate speech.

Ms Mupo emphasised that the President’s focus remains on strengthening the economy, lowering the cost of living and positioning Zambia on the global stage.

“The President has walked the talk before and we believe he will deliver even more this time. His leadership is God-fearing, and his vision is to unite the country while ensuring no one is left behind,” Ms Mupo stated.

She noted that the directive for public servants to dedicate themselves beyond stipulated working hours demonstrates the President’s commitment to accelerating development.

“Work is 24/7, as long as there is work to be done. That is the spirit we must embrace if we are to meet the people’s expectations,” she added.

The District Commissioner further stressed the importance of building a strong and dedicated team to implement government policies effectively, adding that it is vital to have a hardworking team in place to deliver the much-needed development to the people of Zambia.

Ms Mupo reaffirmed Nalolo District’s support for the President’s ideologies and policies, saying the community remains confident in his leadership and vision for the nation.

She further underscored that the Grow Zambia Agenda outlined by the President, focusing on economic expansion, opportunity, and prosperity must be embraced at district level to ensure that every household benefits from national progress.

Meanwhile, Nanjucha Ward Councilor-elect Manyando Mushokabanji has echoed the District Commissioner’s sentiments, describing the President’s speech as a love song for every well-meaning Zambian.

Mr Mushokabanji said the message of unity and inclusiveness provides a strong foundation for development at both national and local levels.

“The President has set the tone for servant leadership. As elected representatives, we must dedicate ourselves to working with the people, respecting one another, and ensuring that development reaches every corner of our communities,” he said.

Both leaders reaffirmed their commitment to supporting the President’s vision, stressing that teamwork and dedication among public servants will be key to delivering the much-needed development in Nalolo District and across the country.

World.title: Chiengi couple burnt to death
World.content:
An elderly couple has died after their grass-thatched house was allegedly set ablaze by unknown people in Chienge district, Luapula Province.

The deceased have been identified as 70 year old John Kaweme and his 65 year old wife, Chilombo Idah, of Kalembwe Kabobo village in Chief Puta’s area.

Luapula Province Police Commissioner Lucky Munkhondya has confirmed the incident, saying it occurred on August 31, 2026, around 01:00 hours.

Ms Munkhondya said police received a report around 02:00 hours from 35 year old Peter Musonda, a nephew to the deceased, who reported that his uncle and aunt had died after their house was set on fire.

She said police officers rushed to the scene and confirmed the incident, where they found the bodies of the couple burnt beyond recognition.

The bodies were retrieved, while police have since opened a docket and commenced investigations to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify those responsible.

World.title: CSDG welcomes Hichilema’s inaugural address
World.content:
Centre for Sustainable Democracy and Governance (CSDG) Executive Director Caroline Katotobwe says President Hakainde Hichilema’s inaugural address, provided hope and confidence that government remains focused on issues affecting ordinary Zambians, particularly the high cost of living.

Dr Katotobwe told the media in an interview today that the President’s declaration that lowering the cost of living is a priority, demonstrates that the government is responsive to the concerns of citizens.

She has called on Zambians to put aside political differences and work collectively towards achieving national development goals.

Dr Katotobwe emphasised that development cannot be achieved when citizens are pulling in different directions, adding that national unity and peace will be essential to delivering tangible benefits at grassroots level.

She has expressed confidence that the second term will focus on implementing programmes whose groundwork was laid during the first five years.

She has also welcomed President Hichilema’s emphasis on unity, peace and inclusivity, saying these are critical foundations for national development.

Dr Katotobwe has since urged Zambians to embrace the President’s call for unity and work towards building a Zambia that benefits both the current and future generations.

World.title: Education sector reacts to President Hichilema’s inauguration speech
World.content:
The National Union of Public and Private Educators of Zambia (NUPPEZ) has welcomed Government’s move to increase investment in education by employing more teachers, constructing additional classrooms and improving teachers’ welfare.

Speaking on the President Hakainde Hichilema’s second-term priorities, NUPPEZ Executive President Charity Kampamba says continued investment in education is essential to producing a skilled population and accelerating national development.

Dr Kampamba stated that the call follows the increase in school enrolment resulting from the introduction of free education, which has placed pressure on existing infrastructure and teaching staff.

She said some classrooms now accommodate between 80 and 90 learners, making it difficult for teachers to effectively manage classes and deliver quality education.

She has called for improved conditions for teachers, particularly those serving in rural areas, saying a motivated workforce is critical to improving the quality of education.

Dr Kampamba further called on the government to ensure that learners have adequate teaching and learning materials, including individual reading materials, instead of sharing books among several pupils.

She commended the UPND administration for its first-term interventions in the education sector, including free education, the recruitment of 30,000 teachers and the expansion of the school feeding programme, adding that the programmes have contributed to increased school enrolment, improved learner retention and greater access to education.

She however, appealed to other stakeholders to complement government efforts in areas such as school construction and the provision of learning materials.

Dr Kampamba has since urged the government to sustain its free education and school feeding programmes while increasing funding towards the construction of classrooms and recruitment of teachers.

Meanwhile, Bridgemark High Schools director Benson Musonda said increased investment will help decongest schools and improve access to quality education, especially in underserved communities.

Mr Musonda congratulated President Hichilema on his re-election and said the sector was encouraged by the renewed focus on education.

He said there is now optimism that the government will scale up infrastructure development, to meet the growing demand for education, following the introduction of free education from Grade One through secondary school.

Mr Musonda has since called for sustained investment in classrooms and other school infrastructure, particularly in rural areas, to ensure learners have access to a conducive learning environment.

World.title: ZANAMACA calls for informal sector focus
World.content:
National Marketers and Traders Association(ZANAMACA) is calling on President Hakainde Hichilema’s administration to place the informal sector at the centre of Zambia’s economic transformation during his second term.

Association President Mupila Kameya said the millions of marketeers, traders, small-scale farmers, bus drivers and taxi operators who sustain livelihoods and facilitate the movement of goods and people deserve greater legal protection, access to finance and meaningful participation in policy-making.

In an exclusive Interview with the media today, Mr Kameya said the government should, as a matter of urgency, fully implement the Markets and Bus Stations Act by establishing and operationalising legal Market and Bus Station Boards across the country.

He said this will help eliminate illegal cadreism, promote transparency in revenue collection and ensure that funds collected from markets are channeled towards improving sanitation, security and infrastructure.

Mr Kameya is further calling for an amendment to the Constituency Development Fund guidelines to ring-fence 2.5 percent of CDF specifically for marketeers, traders and small-scale farmers.

He said such a measure would enable informal economy operators to access affordable micro-capital, equipment and agricultural inputs directly within their communities, without being hindered by bureaucratic processes.

And Mr Kameya has called for deeper collaboration between Government and organisations representing informal sector operators.

He said a structured platform for continuous dialogue and joint decision-making would ensure that policies, urban planning and trade regulations reflect the realities of people operating in markets, farms and bus stations.

Mr Kameya said the informal economy should not be viewed as a burden to be managed, but as an engine of wealth creation capable of contributing significantly to Zambia’s economic development.

He said the success of President Hichilema’s second term should ultimately be measured by whether economic transformation is felt by ordinary Zambians working in markets, farms and bus stations across the country.

World.title: BETUZ Launches Distribution of 90,000 Shirts
World.content:
The Basic Education Teachers Union of Zambia (BETUZ) has launched the distribution of 90,000 shirts to its teacher members ahead of this year’s World Teachers’ Day celebrations slated for October 5, 2026.

BETUZ General Secretary Henry Sinkala said the initiative is aimed at celebrating teachers while reaffirming unity, solidarity, professional pride and the identity of the union.

Dr Sinkala said this in a speech read on his behalf by BETUZ Deputy General Secretary, Christopher Simukonda during the launch at BETUZ Headquarters in Lusaka.

He described the shirts as more than just clothing, stating they symbolised the collective strength and dignity of teachers across the country.

Dr Sinkala said the decision by BETUZ to procure 90,000 shirts also demonstrates how the union values and recognises the contribution of teachers to national development.

He said teachers are not merely employees within the education system, but are architects of the foundation upon which Zambia’s human capital is built.

Dr Sinkala urged teachers to wear the shirts with pride and purpose as a visible declaration of their commitment to the union and the teaching profession.

He announced that distribution of the shirts to provinces would commence immediately following the launch, paving the way for every BETUZ teacher member across the country to receive a shirt.

“A shirt of unity, a symbol of pride, a statement of solidarity,” Dr Sinkala said.

He reaffirmed the Union’s commitment to advocating for issues affecting teachers, including improved remuneration, promotions and upgrades, professional recognition, continuous professional development, better working conditions and improved welfare.

Dr Sinkala said the union will also continue engaging Government and other stakeholders constructively, firmly and consistently to ensure that the welfare, dignity and professional standing of the Zambian teacher remained a national priority.

World.title: Senegal: Senegal and IMF Strike $2.2bn Deal, Two Years After Debt Scandal Froze Funding
World.content:
Senegal and the International Monetary Fund have reached a staff-level agreement on a new $2.2 billion (€1.9 billion) lending programme, nearly two years after an earlier deal was suspended following the discovery of previously unreported public debt.

The 36-month arrangement, announced on Tuesday, is intended to support Senegal's economic and financial reform programme for 2026 to 2029.

However, it still requires approval from the IMF's executive board and depends on Senegal securing financing assurances from international partners.

The deal follows months of negotiations with President Bassirou Diomaye Faye's government, which came to power in 2024 after accusing the administration of former president Macky Sall of concealing the true scale of the country's debt and budget deficit.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Those revelations prompted the IMF to suspend a $1.8 billion (€1.55 billion) programme agreed in 2023 while it sought clarification over Senegal's public finances.

The Fund said the new agreement would require "decisive corrective measures" to address the earlier misreporting.

Finance Minister Cheikh Diba welcomed the breakthrough, saying Senegal and the IMF had reached a technical agreement that "paves the way for financing prospects".

'No blank cheque' for president or government says Senegal's Sonko

Debt burden remains high

Mercedes Vera Martin, a division chief in the IMF's African Department, said the Senegalese authorities had taken steps to improve transparency since the undeclared debt was uncovered.

Those efforts included audits and work to reconcile historical financial data.

Senegal's total public-sector debt was estimated at 132 percent of gross domestic product at the end of 2024, making it one of the most heavily indebted countries in sub-Saharan Africa.

There are, however, signs that the pressure is beginning to ease. The fiscal deficit fell from 13.4 percent of GDP in 2024 to 6.4 percent in 2025, largely as a result of tighter government spending, according to the IMF.

The economy also remained resilient, expanding by 6.7 percent in 2025 as Senegal benefited from its first full year of oil production. Growth outside the hydrocarbon sector was more modest, slowing to 2.2 percent.

Senegal began producing oil from its first offshore field in 2024, providing a new source of growth and revenue as the government works to stabilise the public finances.

The country has meanwhile continued to raise funds on regional markets, although borrowing there is generally more expensive than financing from international institutions and development banks.

Close 

IMF chief outlines plan to resume grants to Senegal

'Debt treatment'

The question of how Senegal should manage its debt has also become politically contentious.

Tensions between Faye and his former prime minister, Ousmane Sonko, intensified earlier this year over several issues, including relations with the IMF.

Faye dismissed Sonko in May, but Sonko later became speaker of the National Assembly, giving him an influential role as reforms linked to the IMF programme move through parliament.

Faye has favoured a more conciliatory approach towards the Fund, while Sonko has rejected conventional debt restructuring.

Asked whether the new programme involved restructuring, Vera Martin said it included "debt treatment", adding that Senegal had developed its own plan.

Diba stressed that the proposal was "not a restructuring in the traditional sense", but an approach designed around Senegal's specific circumstances.

Sonko, however, called for greater transparency in a Facebook post on Tuesday and demanded details of what "debt treatment" would involve.

He also said any commitments would ultimately be debated in the National Assembly, where his Pastef party holds a majority.

The agreement comes after Moody's last week downgraded Senegal's long-term foreign-currency debt rating from Caa1 to Caa2.

World.title: Sudan: Air Attack Destroys Food Aid for Families in South Kordofan
World.content:
A map showing the location of Abyei and Southern Kordofan.

A massive supply of food destined for hungry families in South Kordofan state, Sudan, was destroyed in an aerial attack on two aid trucks over the weekend, the World Food Progamme (WFP) said on Wednesday.

The UN agency strongly condemned the attack which occurred on 30 August outside the city of Dilling.

The trucks carried 50 metric tonnes of WFP food including cereals, yellow split peas, vegetable oil and salt--enough to provide lifesaving assistance to 5,800 people for one month.

They were heading to Kadugli, where WFP is supporting nearly 58,000 people facing emergency levels of food insecurity or worse, and were clearly marked with its banners and flags.

End 'unacceptable' attacks

WFP said the attack was the latest example of the complex operating environment facing it and other humanitarian agencies in Sudan.

The UN has repeatedly called for an end to the war between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and former allies the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) which erupted in April 2023.

As a result of the conflict, some 30 million people required humanitarian assistance last year.

Since January, WFP has recorded eight aerial attacks that have damaged its premises and disrupted operations.

"Attacks on aid workers and humanitarian operations are unacceptable and must stop," WFP said, urging all sides to uphold international humanitarian law by protecting civilians, aid workers and humanitarian assets.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - September 2, 2026
World.content:
Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema Sworn In for Second Term

Zambia's President Hakainde Hichilema has been sworn in for a second five-year term following an election overshadowed by opposition allegations of irregularities and the arrest of his main rival, Brian Mundubile, on treason charges. Hichilema was declared the winner of the 13 August election with 60% of the vote. Mundubile received 38% and claimed the results had been manipulated. Concerns were also raised after courts were sealed off on the final day available for a legal challenge. European Union observers pointed to weaknesses in the vote tallying and verification process. Despite the political tensions, Hichilema used his inauguration to call for unity and urged the opposition to work with his government. His second term comes after five years focused on stabilising Zambia's economy and restructuring its debt. The president is now pledging to shift his attention towards economic growth and prosperity.

Tunisia Faces Growing Crackdown on Civil Society



Tunisia is facing growing concern over what activists and human rights organisations describe as an intensifying crackdown on civil society and political dissent under President Kais Saied. Human Rights Watch said that the authorities have increasingly used arbitrary prosecutions, detentions, financial investigations and the suspension of organisations to silence independent voices and restrict the work of civil society groups. Activists have warned that the uncertainty surrounding possible arrests or prosecutions is creating a climate of fear, causing people to think twice before speaking publicly or working on sensitive issues. Saied, who has rejected accusations of authoritarianism, has defended his actions as necessary to tackle corruption and protect Tunisia's national interests. The crackdown comes amid renewed protests over worsening living conditions, water and electricity shortages and democratic backsliding. Surveys suggest a growing divide between younger Tunisians, who remain more sceptical of state institutions, and older citizens who are more supportive of the government.

DR Congo Schools Reopen Amid Ebola, Conflict and Strike Threat

Millions of students across the Democratic Republic of Congo have returned to school for the new academic year amid major challenges posed by an Ebola outbreak, continuing conflict in the east and a dispute between the government and teachers. The Ebola epidemic has affected six provinces, prompting authorities to introduce a three-tier system under which schools in high-risk areas will shift to limited remote learning. Those in lower-risk zones remain open under different health and safety measures. In territories controlled by the AFC/M23 armed group, schools are reopening under the movement's local authority even though teachers continue to receive their salaries from the government in Kinshasa. At the same time, the country's teachers are divided over whether to return to classrooms. One major union is maintaining a strike call and demanding higher salaries, payment for unpaid staff and improvements to pensions and health insurance. The new school year will therefore test the government's ability to keep children learning despite overlapping health, security and labour challenges.

FBI Confirms Tinubu Was Subject of 1990s Drug Probe

The United States Federal Bureau of Investigation has confirmed in a sworn declaration filed in a federal court that Nigerian President Bola Ahmed Tinubu was the subject of a criminal investigation into drug-trafficking crimes in the early 1990s. The disclosure forms part of an ongoing Freedom of Information Act case seeking the release of FBI records connected to a Chicago heroin-trafficking operation. A court had previously ruled that US agencies could no longer refuse to confirm whether such records existed. However, the FBI's acknowledgement does not establish that Tinubu committed a drug-trafficking offence or was convicted of any crime. Portions of the records remain withheld under exemptions protecting privacy, confidential sources and law-enforcement methods. Tinubu's government has dismissed renewed claims surrounding the records as politically motivated, accusing opposition figures and a Washington-based lobbying firm linked to former vice-president Atiku Abubakar of using decades-old documents to create controversy ahead of Nigeria's 2027 presidential election.

UNICEF Warns 162 Million Children at Risk From Looming El Niño Climate Shocks

UNICEF has warned that more than 162 million children across Eastern and Southern Africa could face severe risks as the strengthening 2026/2027 El Niño brings the threat of droughts, extreme heat and flooding to the region. The UN agency said the climate shocks could worsen food and water insecurity, disrupt healthcare and education. This could leave already vulnerable children exposed to malnutrition, disease, displacement and other dangers across 13 priority countries. Somalia, Ethiopia and South Sudan are among the countries facing particularly serious risks. Existing humanitarian and food crises are likely to be intensified by extreme weather. UNICEF has called for greater investment in anticipatory action, including strengthening nutrition, health and water services, protecting education and expanding social protection before the worst effects are felt. The agency is seeking US$173 million to provide life-saving assistance and warned that acting early could save lives and significantly reduce the costs of responding once a humanitarian crisis has already escalated.

Close 

Nigeria Anti-Corruption Agency Dismisses Over 40 Staff for Financial Misconduct

Nigeria's Economic and Financial Crimes Commission has dismissed more than 40 employees for alleged corruption and financial misconduct over the past three years. Several former staff members are already facing prosecution, and case files are being prepared against others. EFCC chairman Ola Olukoyede said the dismissals were part of efforts to strengthen accountability within an agency tasked with investigating corruption, fraud and money laundering. The commission has also introduced reforms, including renaming its Department of Internal Affairs to the Department of Ethics and Integrity and adopting a policy requiring officers to declare certain gifts and hospitality in an effort to prevent conflicts of interest. Olukoyede said the agency had also recorded significant results since he took office in October 2023, recovering 1.23 trillion naira and securing more than 10,000 convictions. However, the figures also show that the EFCC is increasingly dealing with cybercrime and fraud cases rather than focusing solely on corruption involving high-profile public officials.

World.title: Justin Tucker looks to make NFL comeback after spa allegations, works out with the Jets
World.content:
Justin Tucker was among three kickers who worked out for the New York Jets on Wednesday, according to The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero. Michael Badgley and Joshua Karty also participated in the workout.

Tucker, who is widely considered the greatest kicker in NFL history, has not played since the 2024 season. Last season, Tucker did not sign with a team after serving a 10-game suspension for violating the NFL’s personal conduct policy.

In January 2025, The Baltimore Banner reported that 16 female massage therapists had accused Tucker of sexual misconduct and inappropriate behavior during sessions between 2012 and 2016 at eight spas in and around Baltimore.

The Baltimore Ravens released Tucker in May of that year, after 13 seasons with the franchise.

JUSTIN TUCKER AND WIFE SPEAK OUT AMID MORE ALLEGATIONS FROM MASSAGE THERAPISTS: OUTKICK E

Tucker was never criminally charged or sued civilly over the allegations. He has vehemently denied any wrongdoing.

Tucker, his wife, Amanda, and his legal team spoke exclusively to OutKick the following month. His attorneys, led by Joe Terry of Williams & Connolly, provided information they said cast doubt on the accusations.

Among the material cited by Tucker’s legal team was an email from one accuser who told Tucker it had been "a pleasure working with you" when he canceled his membership at one of the spas in 2016.

That information does not, by itself, prove Tucker’s innocence.

The allegations prompted comparisons to those made against Deshaun Watson. Both cases involved allegations from multiple massage therapists. Watson faced allegations from more than two dozen women and ultimately settled 23 civil lawsuits. He received an 11-game suspension in 2022.

DESHAUN WATSON BOOED BY BROWNS FANS, FIRES BACK AFTER POOR OUTING OPENS DOOR FOR SHEDEUR SANDERS

Despite the allegations, Watson signed the NFL’s first multiyear, fully guaranteed contract with the Cleveland Browns. Five years and $230 million, to be exact.

The Ravens, by contrast, released Tucker after the allegations became public. His future in the NFL is now in doubt.

The difference is that the Browns believed Watson was still a franchise quarterback in his prime. The team was wrong. Watson has never returned to his previous level of play and has become one of the league’s most disappointing starting quarterbacks since.

Tucker’s situation is different. He is a kicker who turns 37 in November and is coming off the worst statistical season of his career. In 2024, he made only 73.3% of his field-goal attempts, a career low.

As usual, multiple statements can be true at once.

Tucker would have had a job last season after his suspension had he still been one of the best kickers in the league. When last seen, he was still better than several kickers in the league.

In any case, NFL teams weigh a player’s baggage, even if unproven, against his performance. To this point, teams have not considered Tucker worth it.

Tucker worked out for the New Orleans Saints and Indianapolis Colts, both of which opted not to sign him.

Justin Tucker did not respond to a request for comment from OutKick on Wednesday. We will update this story if we hear back.

World.title: The primary is over; now come the primetime mistakes
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

There’s a reason football great Deion Sanders was known as "Primetime." Sanders epitomized his sobriquet with electric performances on "Monday Night Football" and in the playoffs.

But not every political candidate is ready for primetime.

The roadside is littered with political failures from both sides. Candidates are better suited for late-night public access in the suburbs.

Consider for a moment someone else who also wasn’t bad in primetime: former football star Herschel Walker. He won the Heisman Trophy in 1982. But when Walker ran for the Senate in Georgia in 2024, his political acumen could barely qualify him for a political practice squad.

UNEARTHED INTERVIEW REVEALS EL-SAYED’S SHARIA ‘OBLIGATION’: ‘NOT BECAUSE OF FEAR’

This year, Democrats trotted out political novice Graham Platner to try to defeat 30-year veteran Sen. Susan Collins, R-Man. But his Nazi-era tattoo and allegations of rape and sexual abuse revealed that Platner was more downtrodden than Down East.

So, how will some of this year’s political hopefuls fare?

Platner would have been the Democrats’ most controversial candidate of the 2026 Senate election cycle. But Michigan Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed has eclipsed Platner.

El-Sayed is progressive. He holds extreme views and previously associated closely with left-wing influencer Hasan Piker.

During an appearance on Fox, El-Sayed compared Sharia law to canon law in the Catholic Church, pitched ditching the Second Amendment and somehow wound up discussing private parts.

El-Sayed’s performance scored headlines. But he also created headaches for Democrats. The party needs to hold the Michigan seat to flip the Senate. And El-Sayed is exactly what Republicans were looking for.

Since El-Sayed captured the Democratic nomination to face former Rep. Mike Rogers, R-Mich., Republicans hope to use him to nationalize the midterms. They want to portray El-Sayed as "what’s wrong" with the Democratic Party and why he’s not aligned with mainstream voters.

The GOP believes that message will trickle down to other Democratic candidates around the country.

In other words, could El-Sayed’s echo undercut Democratic candidates beyond the Wolverine State?

When campaigning, El-Sayed promoted polished policy positions.

"You deserve good health care," said El-Sayed. "You deserve protections at your job."

But when asked on Fox about boys playing sports with girls and sex changes for kids, his rhetoric devolved to this:

"Circumcision is surgery on a kid's ding-a-ling. So, you really want to bring that up? I just think you guys are really selective about how you guys want to talk about things," El-Sayed told Fox’s Jesse Watters.

Political consultants on both sides of the aisle will likely agree. If a candidate finds himself on national television using euphemisms for private parts and not discussing the war in Iran or the cost of groceries, something is wrong.

El-Sayed also backs Medicare-for-all and slavery reparations.

"I just think it's past time to have that conversation. That shouldn't be a crazy thing," said El-Sayed.

Republicans are clamoring to hear more from El-Sayed.

"It's common sense versus communist crazy. And don't believe my word. Listen to what El-Sayed says," House Republican Conference Chairwoman Lisa McClain, R-Mich., told Fox Business.

DEMOCRATS WHO ‘NEVER VOTED REPUBLICAN’ BACK ROGERS OVER EL-SAYED IN RAZOR-CLOSE RACE

El-Sayed’s association with Piker worries Democrats because Piker espouses antisemitic views.

"Those comments were dangerous, malicious and antisemitic and shouldn't be tolerated by anyone in the public square," House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., said.

But now El-Sayed is distancing himself from Piker.

"I got so much exposure and empowerment from the Jewish community," said El-Sayed at a rally. "Jewish people are a light unto the world."

But not everyone is buying it.

"His response was pathetic, and it did not answer the call," Rep. Josh Gottheimer, D-N.J., one of the most pro-Israel Democrats in the House, said on Fox. "This is not a guy who any of us should embrace."

In fact, the campaign of Rogers went as far as to say that El-Sayed was making the case for their candidate.

President Trump recently escalated the trade war with Canada. He renamed Lake Ontario as "Lake America."

El-Sayed vanquished moderate Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., in the primary. With all of this tumult, one wonders if Democrats would feel better wrestling with the president over trade with Stevens as their nominee versus El-Sayed.

That said, politics is a funny thing.

This doesn’t mean that El-Sayed is unelectable. Progressives throb with energy inside the Democratic Party right now. Someone like El-Sayed could actually bolster turnout among the left. This could work to the Democrats’ advantage if Republicans stay home because they’re disappointed in President Trump.

Or, as House Democratic Caucus Vice Chairman Ted Lieu, D-Calif., told voters this week, "Just go fu----- vote."

On the Republican side of the aisle, few had heard of Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C., until brother Sen. Lindsey Graham, R-S.C., died unexpectedly. Republican South Carolina Gov. Henry McMaster quickly appointed Darline to her brother’s seat and cajoled her to run for the full term.

Darline Graham was a political neophyte. And despite President Trump tapping her for the permanent gig, it was far from clear that she was ready for primetime. During a debate in the GOP primary runoff with Rep. Ralph Norman, R-S.C., Graham stumbled when asked about U.S. interests regarding Taiwan.

"I’m not that informed on national security," said Graham. "But I do support the military."

Of course, foreign policy was her brother’s forte. He died just after jetting back to Washington after meetings in Turkey and Ukraine.

But Darline Graham used the gaffe to pivot. She claimed that voters are more concerned with kitchen table issues.

"You know how many (people) brought up Taiwan or national security?" Graham said when stumping. "Not one. They're talking about the rising cost of health care and affordability."

A reporter pressed Graham for details about harnessing inflation.

"Is there something from you, affirmatively (could do like) a piece of legislation, to help drive down the cost of goods?" a scribe asked.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"We'll see when I get there," Graham replied.

Well, Graham is already "here." She’s been in the Senate since mid-July. Some voters could interpret that response as another blunder, perhaps one better suited for Saturday afternoon syndication compared to primetime.

Norman homed in on economics.

"Prices are still too high. Groceries. Gas," said Norman. "(Voters are) feeling it in their pocketbooks."

Darline Graham vanquished Norman in the primary. And barring a major upset by Democratic South Carolina Senate nominee Annie Andrews, Graham is poised to win a full six-year term in the Senate in November.

That’s primetime. Ready or not.

World.title: Emmitt Smith accused of conning Native American investor out of $2.5M in solar farm deal
World.content:
Emmitt Smith, the Pro Football Hall of Fame running back, has been accused of conning a Native American investor out of $2.5 million, a lawsuit filed in Delaware on Monday read.

The lawsuit states that Kituwah LLC, an investment and economic development sector of the Band of Cherokee Indians, loaned $2.5 million after being convinced to join an alleged solar project by Smith, his business partner David Mosley, and 413 Solutions, Inc. – their real estate company, per Front Office Sports.

Kituwah claims that it has not seen "a penny" from the loan, which is more than two years past due. It also alleged that their money loaned was used to pay back a separate company that previously invested in the project.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Project Exodus solar farm was the name of the venture that Kituwah invested in with the understanding it would be named a partner. It alleged the U.S. Department of Energy would be funding the project as well.

Kituwah LLC is seeking at least $2.5 million in damages as well as interest, costs, expenses, and anything else determined during a trial.

FORMER COLLEGE BASKETBALL GUARD KERR KRIISA INDICTED IN ALLEGED $2.2M WIRE FRAUD SCHEME

"Kituwah poured substantial time, efforts, and resources in the purported joint venture," the suit states. "Not only has Kituwah not seen any returns on its investment, Kituwah has been forced to expend additional costs in efforts to reclaim the amounts it is still owed pursuant to its investment, including to investigate what happened to its money."

Kituwah went as far as to say it was "essentially, like a Ponzi scheme," claiming that "false projections and data" were given to them as they made the loan. They also claim that the loan was supposed to be paid back "in a matter of months."

Kituwah said it did an investigation, finding that the money went to Wilson Holdings, which Smith and the other defendants in the lawsuit have partnered with on separate investments.

Smith is the NFL’s all-time leading rusher, tallying 18,355 yards on the ground during his Hall of Fame career, which mostly was spent with the Dallas Cowboys. Smith won three Super Bowls with the franchise across 13 seasons, while playing his final two seasons with the Arizona Cardinals.

Smith also owns the all-time league rushing touchdowns record (164) and rushing first down record (1,028).

World.title: WNBA star will miss playing in FIBA World Cup after her passport goes missing in the mail
World.content:
One of the biggest stress inducers when you travel is keeping tabs on your passport. I’m a lunatic about keeping track of mine because here’s the thing: When I go places, I like to come home again.

Unfortunately for WNBA star Li Yueru of the Dallas Wings, she didn't even get a chance to worry about knowing where her passport was at all times during the 2026 FIBA Women’s World Cup in Berlin.

Why? Because it got lost in the mail.

CAITLIN CLARK AND ANGEL REESE MUST NOW WORK TOGETHER AT WOMEN'S WORLD CUP AS WNBA TAKES A HIGH-STAKES BREAK

The 6-foot-7 center, who led the Chinese national team in points at the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris (obviously, her passport didn't pull a Houdini in the mail that time), revealed that she will not be on the roster when the tournament gets underway.

"Unfortunately, my passport was lost in the mail and still hasn't been found," she wrote in her Instagram story. "Throughout this time, we've all been working hard together and exploring every possible solution, but maybe we were just a little short on luck this time. As of today, the passport is still missing."

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON’T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

That stinks. Sure, it helps teams like the U.S., which is awesome, but you hate to see this.

Unfortunately, you can't control everything, and to quote Carl Showalter, "Things have changed, circumstances, Jerry... force majeure, acts of God."

However, while a lot of us would be shaking with rage if this happened to us, Li Yueru handled it with grace.

"Sometimes, disappointment is simply part of life," the WNBA star wrote. "I'm sad that I won't be able to be there this time, but I'm incredibly grateful for everyone who has supported me and continues to support Chinese women's basketball."

This means that the next time she's on the court for a competitive game will be on Sept. 17, when the Wings return to action with a game against the Los Angeles Sparks.

World.title: Blue state creates six-figure role for trans inmate services amid budget shortfalls
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

The Oregon Department of Corrections (DOC) hired a gender-affirming care coordinator last month, and the job will pay between $78,000 and $115,000 annually.

The job includes oversight of a program for "managing and monitoring needs and safety risks of transgender, intersex and non-binary adults in custody," according to the listing. The position also chairs a multidisciplinary team focused on their individualized needs.

The role, which comes as the DOC is projected to have a $55 million deficit in 2026, continues gender-related initiatives spearheaded by Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek, a longtime champion of the trans community, as she pursues re-election to a second term.

It also highlights the logistical difficulties associated with trans prisoners.

BIOLOGICAL MALE KILLER HOUSED IN OREGON WOMEN'S PRISON WINS HIGH-DOLLAR LEGAL SETTLEMENT IN SEX ABUSE SUIT

After a 2023 review of Oregon’s only women-only prison, the Coffee Creek Correctional Facility, Kotek said her administration would look for ways to address what the report called delayed care for its cisgender and trans inmates.

"Transgender residents [are] being denied or delayed access to needed care, including hormone replacement therapy. This creates significant medical and mental health issues for some residents, including gender dysphoria," the report stated.

The report included one example of a transgender resident at the Coffee Creek who said her request for continuing her hormone blocker treatment had gone unheeded.

"I had been accessing prescriptions at the county. I did not get it when I got here. … I sent several [requests], but they kept bumping me to different places. Now I’ve gotten my period twice. It’s been terrorizing and humiliating," the resident, a biological woman, said.

Kotek promised to address issues raised by the report.

"In the wake of national, systemic shortcomings in meeting the needs of women who are incarcerated, I am resolved to confront these issues head-on," Kotek said in a press release.

FORMER TOP OREGON GOP OFFICIAL SECURES NOMINATION FOR GOVERNOR AS REPUBLICANS TARGET BLUE-STATE PICKUP

"The GIPA report was sobering to read. It is incumbent on Oregon’s corrections system to ensure that the use of carceral settings yield the best possible public safety outcomes and sets people up for successful re-entry."

As a part of the response, her office created the Advisory Panel on Gender Responsive Practices in Corrections.

In turn, the panel recommended training staff who make decisions about housing and medical and behavioral care for the needs of transgender, nonbinary and gender-diverse inmates.

The panel did not specifically recommend the gender-affirming care coordinator position.

The role is similar to a position that would have been established through SB 1120, a failed bill. Among other provisions, that law would have created a role tasked to "provide coordination of efforts and training across staff and adults in custody on best practices for supporting transgender, nonbinary or gender-diverse adults in custody."

The hire clashes with Kotek's instruction to agencies to reduce spending. In 2025, when Republicans in Washington, D.C., passed tax cuts through President Donald Trump's "big beautiful bill," Oregon's tax picture also changed.

The state's tax code mirrors many of the definitions of taxable income used by the federal government. When those definitions shrank, so did Oregon's revenue, leaving the state with a negative general fund balance of $373.7 million, according to state reports.

"This is not what we had planned for, but it is what we must do. I am asking you to leave no stone unturned to save tax-payer dollars. This challenge is not unique to Oregon, but how we respond will be. Our resilience, teamwork and determination have carried us through hard times before. They will again," Kotek wrote in a letter to state department heads.

Like other departments, the DOC was also affected, reporting a projected $55 million deficit. To remedy this, the department was instructed to slow operational spending, prepare for operational cost reductions and suspend non-essential out-of-state travel.

Even so, Kotek has highlighted trans care as a priority, strongly advocating for a government-led approach to expanding access to trans procedures, calling them part of "health care."

"I want to be very clear. Gender-affirming care is health care. Period, end of story," Kotek said at a bill signing in 2023 after the legislature passed a reproductive and gender-affirming care package.

She has also pushed back against attempts from the Trump administration to limit federal funding for hospitals that provide transgender procedures to minors.

TRUMP DIRECTS CMS ADMINISTRATOR MEHMET OZ TO END MEDICAID GENDER TRANSITION FUNDING FOR MINORS

"The Trump administration cannot change the rules and restrict funding to hospitals and doctors who provide gender-affirming care to young people. Gender-affirming care is recognized by major medical organizations and plays an important role in helping young people stay safe, healthy and supported for who they are," Kotek said in a video release.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Kotek’s office did not respond to inquiries from Fox News Digital about the new position and additional details about its duties.

World.title: Vance’s mom fires back at El-Sayed over second family jabs: ‘Probably punch him’
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Vice President JD Vance’s mom, Beverly Vance Aikins, says she’d like to clock Michigan Democratic Senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed after his repeated attacks on the second family.

"I'd probably punch the guy if I ever seen him, and then that would get me in trouble. So, I'll just go with the flow," Aikins told Outkick and Fox News host Tomi Lahren when asked how she felt about El-Sayed’s crude comments.

Aikins sat down with Lahren for a wide-ranging interview about her triumph over opioid addiction, Netflix’s "Hillbilly Elegy" and her son’s rise to the vice presidency.

She made the comments after El-Sayed has repeatedly taken aim at Vance and his family.

VANCE'S DECADE-OLD ‘GREAT REGRETS’ RESURFACES AS EL-SAYED’S JAB AT SECOND LADY COMES BACK TO BITE HIM

Lahren asked Aikins if she laughs off comments like El-Sayed’s or if she gets mad.

"I mean, it makes me mad, honestly, because he doesn't know JD, and he doesn't know, you know, what type of person he is, and I do. But, in the long run. I'm not going to do anything about it. … I'd probably punch the guy if I ever seen him, and then that would get me in trouble," Aikins said in jest.

"So, I'll just go with the flow."

El-Sayed made comments about second lady Usha Vance and the Vance children during an April appearance on "The Allen Analysis Show," clips of which have recently resurfaced.

"I think they're jealous, honestly. I mean, JD is 42 years old. He's handsome. He's the vice president of the United States," Aikins said.

SWING-STATE DEM CANDIDATE'S 'DISGUSTING' COMMENTS ABOUT JD, USHA VANCE'S 'BROWN CHILDREN' SPARKS OUTRAGE

"He's got a beautiful wife, four beautiful children, and jealousy is the only thing I can think of," she added. "I mean, he can take all the shots he wants. It's going to go, you know, it's going to get no merit from any of us."

El-Sayed suggested in April that the vice president's political views are at odds with his own children’s biracial background.

"JD Vance has brown kids who he thinks are less American than everyone else. Like, that's wild to look at your own kids and be like you don’t actually belong as much in this country that I brought you into," said El-Sayed. "Bro, it must break you every time you hug your own kids."

The Michigan socialist said he hopes Vance’s kids grow up to "undo" the vice president’s politics.

SECOND LADY USHA VANCE FIRES BACK AT POINTED JAB FROM DEMOCRATIC SENATE NOMINEE ABDUL EL-SAYED

He also appeared to call for the second lady to leave her husband, saying, "Usha get out … you’ve still got time."

El-Sayed more recently launched the attack after JD Vance slammed him for his stated adherence to Sharia law during a rally in Ohio, suggesting the practice would be completely alien to his grandfather, whom he calls his "Papaw."

VANCE UNLOADS ON EL-SAYED OVER SHARIA REMARKS: ‘THAT’S NOT MY GRANDPA’S DEMOCRATIC PARTY’

"So, do we think JD is taking Usha with him back in time to meet Papaw, or no," El-Sayed said, seemingly in reference to the second lady's Indian ethnicity.

The vice president addressed El-Sayed’s more recent remarks while rallying for GOP Senate nominee Mike Rogers in Michigan.

"I actually think that the people of Michigan think it's kind of weird when you talk about another guy's wife," Vance said.

"But whatever you want to talk about, Abdul, keep my wife's name the hell out of your mouth, because she's way out of your league," he later added in the speech.

World.title: Colin Kaepernick believes Jay-Z has a ‘guilty conscience’ over deals with NFL and Target
World.content:
Colin Kaepernick said he believes that Jay-Z’s recent comments about him speak to a “guilty conscience,” as the fallout between the former quarterback and the rapper deepens. Kaepernick responded as part of an extensive interview with NBC News after Jay-Z dissed the athlete during a recent concert.

In July, Jay-Z took aim at Kaepernick, the former San Francisco 49ers star, mentioning him and his settlement with the NFL in an impromptu rap during a series of concerts at Yankee Stadium.

“They run out of characters, had to bring back up [Kaepernick] again,” Jay-Z said, referring to people who have criticized him for a recent partnership with Target. “Buddy took a check, I ain’t even mad at him, but along with that check you have to sign a non-disparagement. I’m the one [the NFL] can’t control.”

Earlier this year, Jay-Z drew ire when it was announced that he would sell an exclusive version of his “Reasonable Doubt” album at the retailer, which has been subjected to boycotts by Black shoppers after it rolled back its diversity, equity and inclusion practices.

Kaepernick, on the other hand, is honoring the boycott despite the potential financial cost. A spokesperson for the former quarterback confirmed he would not be selling his upcoming memoir, “The Perilous Fight,” in Target stores. Target did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

For his book tour, Kaepernick is partnering with the National Association of Black Bookstores.

More Colin Kaepernick coverage on NBC News Kaepernick will be the first guest on “Before & After with Lester Holt,” available as soon as Sept. 7.

Kaepernick is set to appear on “TODAY” on Sept. 16.

Jay-Z was freestyling about the hypocrisy of his critics in July when he mentioned Kaepernick. The lyrics were a far cry from 2017, when Jay-Z dedicated a performance of his song “The Story of O.J.” to Kaepernick after he had taken a knee to protest police brutality in America.

At the time, Kaepernick was a free agent. He never found employment in the NFL again after he protested during the national anthem in the 2016 season. Jay-Z, who wore Kaepernick’s jersey during a performance on “Saturday Night Live” in 2017, was one of Kaepernick’s highest-profile supporters.

Jay-Z was critical of the NFL, rapping on the 2018 song “Apes---” with his wife, Beyoncé, “I said no to the Super Bowl. You need me; I don’t need you.”

In his book, Kaepernick wrote that Jay-Z asked him in 2017 to kneel onstage during a performance of “The Story of O.J.” but that he declined, in part because he objected to the use of racial slurs in the lyrics. Kaepernick also wrote that before he was asked to join Jay-Z onstage, he had difficulties connecting with him on the phone as they exchanged emails in an effort to join forces on social justice issues.

Their relationship flipped in August 2019, when Jay-Z announced that Roc Nation, the entertainment company he co-founded, would partner with the NFL. Roc Nation has since produced every Super Bowl halftime show, and it partners with the league on social justice work.

Roc Nation declined to comment to NBC News for this article.

In his book, Kaepernick wrote that Jay-Z told him about the partnership only after it had been agreed to, and Kaepernick expressed his displeasure.

“I just want you to know, one, you’re serving the culture up to a bunch of racists and, two, they don’t care about you,” Kaepernick wrote about what he told Jay-Z when they spoke. “You’re the music guy to them. They quite literally need a Black face—and have said as much.”

In 2019, Jay-Z faced blowback for the NFL deal, as many viewed it as his turning his back on Kaepernick, who remained unemployed by the league.

At a news conference announcing the partnership, Jay-Z defended the decision.

“I think we have moved past kneeling. I think it’s time for action,” he said. “We forget that Colin’s whole thing was to bring attention to social injustice. In that case, this is a success. This is the next phase.”

The NFL declined to comment.

Kaepernick, who told NBC News’ Lester Holt that he did not sign a non-disparagement agreement with the NFL after having settled in 2019 with the league over his collusion lawsuit, said several people sent him the video of the freestyle.

“First and foremost, what it speaks to is power of people,” Kaepernick said about his reaction. “The backlash that [Jay-Z] received for partnering with the NFL and going counter to people’s interests in 2019 was a major problem for him, so much so that he’s still bringing it up in 2026.”

He added: “People are now realizing, ‘Why are you so comfortable stepping into these positions that are counter to the positions that people on the ground actually want?’ And to me, I view that as speaking to a guilty conscience and trying to reposition or reframe the conversation.”

Kaepernick said people who supported him have been consistent in not agreeing with Jay-Z’s actions.

“I haven’t publicly spoken about him in any matter, but it speaks to the level of impact that people are having and being able to continue to move not only individuals but corporations,” he said.

As for why he didn’t respond to Jay-Z immediately after the freestyle, particularly in regard to the misinformation about a non-disparagement agreement, Kaepernick said that there have always been efforts to discredit him and that Jay-Z is “another player” in that effort since he partnered with the NFL.

“He has built the alignment with the NFL, the NFL that has blackballed me, the same NFL that, in a players-owners meeting in 2017, said we need a Black face to help us get rid of the protests,” Kaepernick told NBC News. (The NFL has long denied Kaepernick’s blackballing claims.)

Kaepernick added: “I understand why he’s trying to do reputational recovery. I get it. I don’t agree with the actions, but I’m also not gonna respond to everything that’s said about me, because I also believe the actions and the work that I do will speak for themselves.”
