NEW DELHI: A day after NCLT barred him from alienating any of his property and stayed its order allowing him to settle his personal insolvency proceedings by paying around Rs 6.3 crore as against admitted claims of Rs 22,006.5 crore, Zee Group founder Subhash Chandra questioned the validity of the order before NCLAT. He alleged the tribunal did not have the power to constitute a five-member special bench, as was done to decide his case.Senior advocate Sasmit Patra, appearing for Chandra, submitted before an NCLAT bench of officiating chairperson Justice Yogesh Khanna and technical members Barun Mitra and Ajai Das Mehrotra that the order was "faulty and wrong"."The scope of Section 419(5) is very limited. If there is a differing view, then that differing view has to be taken up by another member... It does not empower NCLT under IBC or company law to form a five-member bench... Under which power? When did this five-member bench sit together?" he submitted.The appellate tribunal was hearing appeals filed by Union Bank of India (UK), Canara Bank and LIC Housing Finance against the Aug 25 opinion approving Chandra's repayment plan.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta, appearing for the creditors, submitted that the petition filed against the third member's order "may be disposed of with liberty to revive it" since some respondents could challenge the reference itself.Patra raised a grievance that Chandra had been vilified across the country over a proposed payment of Rs 6.5 crore. World.title: Government bodies differ, Centre to test green crackers afresh
World.content:
NEW DELHI: As two govt organisations took contradictory stands on commercial production of next-generation green firecrackers - with Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-NEERI approving new formulations and Central Pollution Control Board objecting - Centre Wednesday told Supreme Court that it intended to conduct fresh tests to assess the harmful impact of the use of barium.

Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati told a bench of Justices M M Sundresh and Augustine George Masih that govt, after consulting stakeholders, had decided to conduct the tests in New Delhi, Bhopal, Kolkata and Chennai.

Centre had asked CSIR-NEERI to develop green/low-emission fireworks - with particulate matter (PM) emission reduction of more than 50% - in association with manufacturers. Tamil Nadu Fireworks and Amorces Manufacturers' Association (Tanfama) devised new-generation formulation crackers with a reduced quantity of barium salts/nitrates in combination with other oxidisers.

In a report, CSIR-NEERI said with the new formulations, emission reductions achieved for PM10 and PM2.5 were between 45% and 60%, and recommended that the formulations for light-emission fireworks (such as flowerpots, sparklers, chakkars, pencils, twinkling stars and their hybrids) be considered for commercial production.

It also approved the manufacture of 'joined crackers', known as 'ladis', which have been banned by a court order.





The report said there was a reduction in PM emissions by approximately 30% and a reduction in solid waste generation by up to 32% for joined crackers.

CPCB asked how barium nitrate could be used in crackers when it was banned by SC. "This court, vide order dated Oct 23, 2018, has expressly banned the use of barium salts in firecrackers and, therefore, any formulation involving barium compounds, even in reduced quantities, is in contravention of the said order," it said in its communication to govt.

World.title: Farakka Treaty renewal will have Bihar in mind: EAM
World.content:
Centre has assured Bihar that any decision will be made keeping in mind the state's water requirements

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: With India looking at different issues before taking a call on renewing its treaty with Bangladesh over sharing of Ganga river waters at Farakka Barrage, Centre has assured Bihar that any decision will be made keeping in mind the state's water requirements for drinking and industrial use.The assurance came from Union external affairs minister S Jaishankar in response to concerns first raised by former chief minister Nitish Kumar during his tenure and recently by his JDU colleague and party national working president Sanjay Jha.RS MP Jha had raised the issue in the Upper House on Aug 6, seeking protection of Bihar's water interests in any renewal of the 30-year-old treaty, signed in 1996 and set to expire in Dec. He has opposed the renewal of the Farakka Treaty, alleging it has done "great injustice" to Bihar over the past three decades.In a letter to Jha, Jaishankar said govt "fully" understands the state's concerns regarding the treaty and will make a decision keeping the relevant considerations in mind. He said that inter-ministerial discussions led by jal shakti ministry had been held with stakeholders to comprehensively discuss the implementation and future of the treaty.

World.title: 2 Kuki-Zo MLAs set foot in Imphal for 1st time in 3 years
World.content:
GUWAHATI: Two Kuki-Zo MLAs travelled to Imphal Wednesday in defiance of a community whip and attended the Manipur assembly session in person for the first time since violence erupted in 2023, creating a hill-valley divide that is still to be bridged.

Saikul legislator Kimneo Haokip Hangshing of Kuki Peoples' Alliance (KPA) and Independent MLA Haokholet Kipgen of Saitu, both in Kangpokpi district, chose to be in the assembly for the first day of the session despite Kuki Inpi Manipur's explicit instruction to stay away from Meitei-majority Imphal.

Deputy CM Nemcha Kipgen and her BJP colleague, Henglep MLA Letzamang Haokip, attended the session over videoconferencing.

Other four Kuki-Zo MLAs from BJP abstained. Manipur has nine Kuki-Zo MLAs, including two from KPA. Six of them had attended the budget session last Feb virtually.

CM Y Khemchand Singh's office issued a statement lauding the two Kuki MLAs for making what it termed a "historic physical return" to the assembly. "Their attendance comes after a gap of three and a half years, during which representatives from the community had not physically participated in person in House proceedings," it said.

Singh attributed the MLA duo's "positive step" to BJP-led govt's efforts to reduce the trust deficit among communities. "With collective efforts, Manipur can strive to walk the path to peace," Singh said.

Kuki Inpi Manipur has barred elected community representatives from venturing into Imphal Valley until Union and state govts accede to their demand for a separate administration for the hills.

While violence involving Kuki and Meitei communities has ebbed, Manipur is firefighting escalating tensions between Naga and Kuki groups in the hills, mainly along the Imphal-Tamenglong Road corridor in Kangpokpi. Since May 13, at least 17 people from Kuki-Zo and Naga communities have died in instances of violence along the Kangpokpi-Tamenglong stretch.

World.content:
The death toll from the devastating Nepal-Tibet flash floods surged to 1,243 on Wednesday (September 2, 2026), as rescuers battled rain and debris to trace those believed to be trapped in the tunnels along the course of the Bhotekoshi river and underground powerhouses in the Himalayan nation.

Watch | How a school in Nepal saved 900 students from a devastating flash flood

World.title: How valuable are mangroves? Study on Pichavaram ecosystem pegs it at ₹2,485.38 crore
World.content:
Ecosystem service-wise economic value (in ₹ crore) Provisioning services (Fish, Crab, Shrimp): 3.47 Coastal protection function: 147.17 Nutrient cycling: 10.53 Oxygen regulation: 181.22 Carbon sequestration (annual flow): 26.86 Biodiversity conservation: 19.48 Recreational and tourism value: 484.25 Carbon stock value (vegetation): 387.77 Soil organic carbon: 1224.63 Total Economic Value (TEV): 2,485.38

How valuable are mangroves? A recent study of the Pichavaram mangrove ecosystem estimated its Total Economic Value (TEV) at ₹2,485.38 crore ($289 million), with a per-hectare value of ₹1.83 crore, reflecting the ecological, economic and social benefits it provides.

The Pichavaram Mangrove Forest is deemed one of the most ecologically significant coastal wetland ecosystems in India and plays a vital role in supporting biodiversity conservation, fisheries productivity, coastal protection, climate regulation, blue carbon sequestration, and livelihood security for coastal communities.

“Mangrove ecosystems provide a wide range of provisioning, regulating, supporting, and cultural ecosystem services that contribute significantly to ecological sustainability and human well-being. Despite their importance, many ecosystem services remain undervalued in conventional development planning because several ecological benefits are non-market in nature and are not reflected in market transactions,” says the study, ’Economic Valuation and Blue Carbon Assessment of Ecosystem Services (ESV) in the Pichavaram Mangrove Forest’.

Increasing climate change impacts, biodiversity loss, and coastal vulnerability have further emphasised the need for comprehensive assessment of the ecological and economic contributions of mangrove ecosystems, it added.

In 2024, the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), in what it termed the“first global assessment of a full ecosystem functional group across the planet using the Red List of Ecosystems,” said 50% of mangrove ecosystems in the world are at risk of collapse.

The study, by M. Balasubramanian, associate professor, Centre for Ecological Economics and Natural Resources, Institute for Social and Economic Change, Bengaluru, was funded by the Deputy Conservator of Forests, Forest Genetics Division, Coimbatore. It was based on primary and secondary data; primary information was collected from 302 households across five mangrove-dependent villages: MGR Thittu, Kalaignar Nagar, Chinnavaikal, Patriadi, and Mudasalodai.

Carbon reservoir

“The blue carbon assessment highlights the critical role of the Pichavaram Mangrove Ecosystem as a significant natural carbon sink and a valuable climate regulation asset. Field measurements and carbon stock analysis indicated that the mangrove vegetation stores an average of 79.449 tonnes of carbon per hectare, equivalent to approximately 291.33 tonnes of CO2 per hectare,” says the study.

The analysis further revealed that mangrove sediments constitute an even more substantial carbon reservoir. The average soil organic carbon stock of 251.14 tonnes of carbon per hectare was estimated to generate an economic value of ₹90.24 lakh per hectare, resulting in a total soil organic carbon value of ₹1,224.63 crore. When vegetation and soil carbon pools are combined, the total blue carbon asset value of the Pichavaram Mangrove Ecosystem is estimated at ₹1,612.40 crore

“These findings clearly demonstrate that the majority of blue carbon is stored below ground in mangrove sediments, emphasising the importance of conserving both mangrove vegetation and soil systems. The substantial blue carbon value underscores the ecosystem’s contribution to climate regulation, carbon sequestration, and long-term ecological sustainability, while also providing strong justification for integrating mangroves into climate finance mechanisms, blue carbon initiatives, and natural capital accounting frameworks,” the study added.

Integration

The study recommends the integration of ecosystem service valuation into coastal development planning and environmental decision-making, recognition of mangroves as critical nature-based solutions for climate adaptation and disaster risk reduction, and the development of blue carbon financing mechanisms, carbon credit programmes, and Payment for Ecosystem Services (PES) schemes.

It also advocates the incorporation of mangrove values into the Natural Capital Accounting and Green GDP frameworks, the promotion of sustainable livelihood opportunities through fisheries, eco-tourism, community-based conservation, and mangrove restoration, and strengthening climate resilience and biodiversity conservation through long-term ecosystem-based management strategies.

World.title: Five dead, 30 injured in bus-truck collision in M.P.’s Rewa
World.content:
Five persons were killed and 30 others injured after a bus collided with a truck on a national highway in the Rewa district of Madhya Pradesh on Wednesday (September 2, 2026), police said.

The accident took place around 4:30 p.m. on National Highway 39 near Badwar, located under the Gudh police station area, about 30 kilometres from the district headquarters, a senior official said.

The accident scene dissolved into chaos as the victims’ screams filled the air. Locals immediately began relief work and informed the police.

Soon after being informed, police and administration teams arrived at the scene and launched relief and rescue operations. Several ambulances were dispatched to transport the injured to the hospital.

Additional Superintendent of Police (ASP) Bhavana Maravi told PTI Videos, “Five people died in the accident, while 30 others were injured.” She said all the injured were shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital in Rewa, where they are undergoing treatment.

Rescue operations are still underway at the scene, and efforts are on to ensure that nobody is trapped in the bus, she said.

Maravi said the impact was so severe that the truck overturned and the bus fell into a water-filled drain.

Chief Minister Mohan Yadav expressed grief over the accident and said the state government has issued instructions to provide financial assistance of ₹2 lakh each to the families of the deceased and ₹1 lakh each to the seriously injured.

In a post on X, he said, “The news of the deaths of passengers in the collision between a bus and a dumper on the Rewa-Sidhi highway today is extremely heartbreaking. I pray for the peace of the departed souls and a speedy recovery for the injured.” Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) Anurag Tiwari said additional beds have been reserved in the hospital so that other injured people can also be treated immediately if required.

The police are investigating the cause of the accident, he said.

National Highway 39 connects Jhansi in Uttar Pradesh to Ranchi, the capital of Jharkhand, and passes through Madhya Pradesh.

World.title: West Asia conflict updates: Iran blacklists more ships trying to sail through Hormuz, govt. website shows
World.content:
Iran threatened to take a tougher line in its war with the United States on Wednesday (September 2, 2026) after the heaviest exchanges in weeks left at least 19 Iranians dead, including four at a wedding -- an incident slammed as a “war crime” by Tehran. A wave of Iranian attacks earlier targeted US bases in Jordan, the UAE, Kuwait, Bahrain and Iraq’s autonomous Kurdistan region, after extensive U.S. bombardment hit sites across Iran.

Watch | U.S., Iran exchange fresh strikes near Strait of Hormuz

U.S. President Donald Trump had warned earlier of “much harder and higher” attacks if Iran retaliated to the U.S. strikes, which Iran’s military and state media said killed 18 people. U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) spokesperson Tim Hawkins said “the U.S. military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC”, referring to Iran’s Revolutionary Guards.

The latest flare-up is part of a cycle of retaliation that followed U.S. strikes on Iran, with fighting over the Hormuz strait expanding to Washington’s Gulf allies, military bases and commercial shipping. It began when Washington hit Iranian targets on Sunday (August 30, 2026), the first known strikes in several weeks, after which Tehran’s forces targeted US troops in Jordan and the United Arab Emirates, and projectiles struck two oil tankers in unclaimed attacks.

(With inputs from agencies)

World.title: Morning Digest: Jaishankar says Bihar’s concerns will be considered before Ganga treaty renewal; Trump floats renaming Strait of Hormuz as ‘Trump Strait’, and more
World.content:
Trump floats renaming Strait of Hormuz as ‘Trump Strait’

U.S. President Donald Trump on Wednesday (September 2, 2026) suggested renaming the Strait of Hormuz as “Trump Strait” even though the crucial waterway remains contested amid the war with Iran. “Now that we have it under U.S.A. control, should we change the name Hormuz Strait to TRUMP STRAIT??? Like America itself, it would be ‘hotter’ than ever before!” Mr. Trump said on his Truth Social network.

Will consider Bihar’s concerns before Ganga treaty renewal, says Jaishankar

India will decide on the renewal of the 1996 Ganga Water Treaty while keeping Bihar’s interests in consideration, stated External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar in a recent letter to Janata Dal (U) MP Sanjay Jha, who had called upon the government not to renew the treaty, asserting that it had “negatively impacted” the State. The India-Bangladesh Ganga Water Treaty will expire on December 31, 2026. Renewal of the treaty is one of the major items on this year’s diplomatic calendar of the two countries.

Supreme Court seeks explanation from government on IPS deputation in CAPFs

The Supreme Court on Wednesday (September 2, 2026) sought an explanation from Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan on the implementation of its May 2025 judgment directing the Centre to progressively reduce the deputation of Indian Police Service (IPS) officers to senior posts in the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs). While hearing the contempt petition filed by retired CAPF officers, Justice Ujjal Bhuyan orally observed that there was a “strong lobby” and the cadre officers of CAPFs are “completely stifled”.

Allahabad HC quashes NSA detention of student, calls case ‘concocted story’

The Allahabad High Court on Wednesday (September 2, 2026) quashed the detention of Delhi University law student Akriti Chaudhary under the National Security Act (NSA). The 25-year-old has spent nearly five months in custody over the workers’ protest in Noida in April this year.

Mallojula Venugopal Rao alias Bhupati: From dreaded Maoist to Gondwana University coordinator in Gadchiroli

Life has taken a 180-degree turn for Bhupathi alias Abhay alias Mallojula Venugopal alias Sonu. He was once a dreaded Maoist, who had a bounty of ₹6 crore on his head, with the police of six different States chasing him. Less than a year after surrendering before the Maharashtra Police, an event that had led to the breaking of the back of Maoism in Maharashtra, the 70-year-old man now looks at a different future.

Gurugram MP seeks action-report on encroachments, warns of CBI probe into waterlogging

Union Minister of State and Gurugram MP Rao Inderjit Singh on Wednesday expressed regret to residents affected by the recent waterlogging and said a permanent solution would require restoring the city’s natural drainage system, maximising rainwater harvesting and recharging groundwater.

West Bengal government using police against Opposition, says TMC MP

Trinamool Congress Rajya Sabha MP Sagarika Ghose on Wednesday (September 2, 2026) accused the BJP-led administration in West Bengal of misusing the police and law-and-order machinery to target Opposition leaders, describing it as an assault on democracy, constitutional values, and human rights.

Nepal Floods: Death toll near 1,250 as more than 4,000 still missing

The death toll has surged to 1,222 as more bodies were recovered from eight districts affected by the flood, while 4,875 people remain missing a week after the floods devastated several towns and villages in the country, according to Nepal Police. Security forces have recovered 348 dead bodies from Chitawan district, 218 from Nawalparasi East, 208 from Nawalparasi West, and 155 from Nuwakot. Similarly, 127 bodies were recovered from Rasuwa, 69 from Gorkha, 60 from Dhading and 38 from Tanahu, according to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.

India to stage inaugural Women’s Champions Trophy 2027 after Sri Lanka dropped as host

The International Cricket Council on Wednesday (September 2, 2026) moved the inaugural Women’s Champions Trophy to India from Sri Lanka, and the six-team event will be played in Mumbai and Vadodara from February 14 to 28. Sri Lanka was dropped as the host as the sport is grappling with governance issues in the island nation. The ICC Board approved India as the new host on Wednesday (September 2).

World.title: Two dead, multiple injured in Minneapolis shooting
World.content:
Two people have died and several more were injured, including three police officers, when a gunman opened fire in the U.S. city of Minneapolis on Wednesday (September 2, 2027), police said.

The suspect was also dead, Garrett Parten, a spokesperson for the police, said at a press conference, adding that it wasn’t clear how he had died.

One person died at the scene, Parten added. Four people were taken to hospital, where one later died.

Also taken to the hospital were three police officers, including two who were shot. Both were expected to survive, with a hospital spokesperson telling AFP that they were in “stable condition”.

One was shot in the leg, while another was in surgery. It was not clear what injury the third officer sustained.

There was no mention of motive during the press conference.

Governor Tim Walz asked the public to “pray for Minnesota”, while FBI Director Kash Patel said his agents were responding.

City officials are expected to hold a press conference later on Wednesday (September 2, 2027).

World.title: Plane carrying U.S. DHS chief lands after suffering engine failure
World.content:
A U.S. Coast Guard-operated Gulfstream V ​jet carrying Homeland ⁠Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin safely diverted to Reagan Washington National Airport on ‌Wednesday (September 2, 2026) after suffering an engine failure.

The pilot declared ‌an emergency after ‌the ⁠right engine failed on a ⁠flight from Atlanta to the Washington, D.C., area and landed at Reagan, according ​to Mullin ‌and air traffic control audio.

The C-37A plane had 14 people on board, according to the pilot. It ‌landed around 1:35 p.m. ​ET (1735 GMT)

“The United States Coast Guard pilots ⁠made the single engine landing feel routine,” Mullin said on ‌X. “No panic, just straight professionalism.” He added: “After we landed, the pilots told me that was a first for them! We could not have ‌been in better hands.”
