The National Bank of Georgia says the measure aims to protect vulnerable customers, particularly older people, from fraud.

The idea is simple: if a fraudster convinces someone to make an urgent transfer, the 48-hour pause gives them additional time to consider whether they really want to go ahead with the transaction.

According to the National Bank, a similar approach is used in other countries, including the US, Canada, Brazil, the UK and EU member states.

The new rule therefore does not ban people over 60 from making bank transfers. Instead, it temporarily suspends transactions that appear suspicious based on a number of indicators. This gives customers another opportunity to reconsider their decision before falling victim to fraud or losing their money.

World.title: Uzbekistan's industrial output increases by almost 8% in Jan-July 2026
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 3. Uzbekistan's industrial production reached 795.4 trillion soums (about $67.3 billion) in January-July 2026, with industrial output increasing 7.9% from the same period a year earlier.

This was reflected in the statement by the National Statistics Committee of Uzbekistan.

Manufacturing remained the dominant component of Uzbekistan's industrial sector, accounting for 86.8% of total output. Mining and quarrying represented 6.3%, electricity, gas, steam and air conditioning supply accounted for 6.4%, while water supply, sewerage, waste collection and disposal made up the remaining 0.5%.

The manufacturing sector was the main driver of industrial expansion, with output increasing 9% year on year. Electricity, gas, steam and air conditioning production rose 8.1%, while water supply, sewerage and waste management increased 8.4%.

Trend's calculations show that manufacturing generated approximately 690 trillion soums (around $38.4 billion) of industrial output during the seven-month period, based on its 86.8% share of total production. Electricity and gas-related activities accounted for about 51 trillion soums, while mining and quarrying contributed roughly 50 trillion soums (approx. $4.2 billion).

Within manufacturing, the strongest increases were recorded in the production of machinery and equipment not elsewhere classified, which rose 1.5 times, and leather and related products, which increased 1.4 times compared with January-July 2025.

At the same time, several manufacturing segments recorded declines. Production of tobacco products fell to 89.9% of the level recorded a year earlier, while output from enterprises engaged in the repair and installation of machinery and equipment declined to 81.6% of the January-July 2025 level.

In Trend's assessment, the composition of industrial growth points to a continued shift toward higher-value manufacturing and equipment production. The 50% increase in machinery and equipment output is particularly significant because it suggests that industrial expansion is not being driven solely by traditional resource-based sectors.

Trend's analysis also shows that manufacturing's 86.8% share of industrial production gives changes in this sector an outsized influence on overall industrial performance. The 9% increase in manufacturing therefore provides the main foundation for the country's 7.9% overall industrial growth, while the simultaneous expansion of utilities and waste-management activities indicates broader industrial and infrastructure demand.

The decline in tobacco production and machinery repair and installation, however, shows that industrial growth remains uneven across subsectors. The contrasting performance suggests that investment and production capacity are increasingly concentrated in selected manufacturing activities, particularly machinery and equipment and other industries with expanding demand.

Overall, Uzbekistan's industrial sector maintained solid growth in the first seven months of 2026, with output approaching 800 trillion soums (about $67.7 billion). The dominance of manufacturing and its faster-than-average expansion, combined with rapid growth in machinery production, points to continued industrial diversification, although weaker performance in some subsectors remains a factor to watch.

World.title: Tajikistan’s retail trade gains strong momentum in 1H2026
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 3. The retail trade turnover in Tajikistan reached 38.3 billion somoni ($4.15 billion) in the first half of 2026.

According to data from the Interstate Statistical Committee of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), retail trade turnover in Tajikistan increased by 35.9% in constant prices from January through June 2026 compared with the same period of 2025.

In June 2026, retail trade turnover grew by 48.7% in constant prices compared with June 2025, while increasing by 12.4% compared with May 2026.

For comparison, retail trade turnover in Tajikistan increased by 5.1% in the first half of 2025 compared with the same period of 2024.

Furthermore, in June 2025, the indicator decreased by 5.1% year-on-year and by 8.3% compared with May 2025.

The Trend’s analysis indicates that Tajikistan’s retail trade sector accelerated significantly in the first half of 2026, pointing to stronger consumer activity and an expansion in domestic demand.

The sharp improvement compared with the previous year suggests that retail trade has become a more significant contributor to economic activity. The particularly strong year-on-year growth recorded in June also indicates that the sector maintained its momentum toward the middle of the year.

The monthly increase in June further points to an expansion in consumer spending during the period. At the same time, the sustainability of this trend will depend on household income growth, price dynamics, employment conditions, and the availability of consumer goods.

The acceleration in retail activity may also support related sectors, including wholesale trade, transport, logistics and services, while providing additional opportunities for businesses operating in Tajikistan’s domestic market.

World.title: Scurvy listed as most likely factor in 6yo Qld boy's death
World.content:
A coroner has found scurvy to be the "most likely underlying factor" in the death of a Queensland boy with Down syndrome.

Six-year-old Connor Dean died in the Queensland Children's Hospital on August 10, 2024, after his heart stopped following a general anaesthetic, and he experienced a severe brain injury from a lack of oxygen.

He weighed just 14.1kg when he died.

In non-inquest findings, Deputy Queensland Coroner Stephanie Gallagher, backed a forensic pathologist's opinion that Connor died from "hypoxic ischaemic encephalopathy due to cardiac arrest following general anaesthetic, in the setting of vitamin C deficiency".

She found Down syndrome was a "contributing factor".

"Although the precise mechanism leading to the cardiac arrest could not be definitively determined, the treating clinicians and forensic pathologist considered vitamin C deficiency to be the most likely underlying factor," Ms Gallagher wrote.

Connor had surgery as a baby for a heart defect, was developmentally delayed and communicated using "mostly single words".

He walked and ran with a "wide-based gait".

About a month before his death, his parents reported he started walking with a "shuffling gait which progressed to limping" and eventually he refused to weight bear.

Scurvy a 'likely unifying diagnosis'

He was admitted to the Queensland Children's Hospital for investigation, which included a scan under general anaesthetic.

He went into cardiac arrest following the scan and was revived after 8-10 minutes of cardio-pulmonary resuscitation (CPR).

As his condition deteriorated and opinions were sought from various specialists, his family was told "severe life-threatening scurvy (vitamin C deficiency) seemed a likely unifying diagnosis".

His parents said they were unaware of their son's Vitamin C deficiency until after his cardiac arrest.

Connor's paediatrician, who had about 20 years' experience in the specialty, told Ms Gallagher in a statement he had "significant concerns regarding Connor's growth and nutritional deficiencies for a long time".

In November 2023, he said he discussed with Connor's mother that the boy's diet was inadequate to meet his vitamin and mineral requirements" but he believed his needs were being met with his intake of multivitamin supplements.

During Connor's admission just before his death, his mother advised he was taking a multivitamin and his immunisations were up to date.

Connor's paediatrician told the coroner he was concerned the product, which was not named in Ms Gallagher's findings, was available in Australia.

"I believe that it is misleading to call this product a multivitamin when it misses essential vitamins such as Vitamin C," the medical specialist said.

Given the absorption of plant-based iron is greatly enhanced by Vitamin C, he said it was "illogical" to have an iron-containing product in combination with multiple vitamins, but not Vitamin C.

"It is my clinical opinion that Connor would not have had Vitamin C deficiency, and the clinical features of scurvy that lead to his death, if he had been taking a different multivitamin that contained Vitamin C," the paediatrician said.

But the manufacturer of the multivitamin told Ms Gallagher in response: "Multivitamin products do not generally contain all essential vitamins and nor are they indicated for treatment of a severe deficiency.

"They are indicated to help supplement when dietary intake is inadequate."

The manufacturer told the coroner that given "the apparent lack of monitoring of Connor's Vitamin C deficiency prior to his arrest, there is no basis on which to draw the conclusion that" the multivitamin contributed to Connor's death.

"Any such uncertainty should not be resolved by the adoption of a single clinical opinion by a non-independent clinician in the circumstances," the manufacturer wrote.

Ms Gallagher did not address the multivitamin issue in her conclusions.

"The evidence establishes that Connor Dean had severe Vitamin C deficiency, with associated … features consistent with scurvy, and that he suffered a cardiac arrest following the administration of a general anaesthetic," she wrote.

"I extend my condolences to Connor's family and loved ones for their loss."

World.title: Zoo's baby chimpanzee to be sent elsewhere after mother's rejection
World.content:
A central Queensland zoo will send a baby chimpanzee elsewhere after a failed reunion with its mother.

Female chimp Sile gave birth to Cassie at the Rockhampton Zoo in June, but dropped the baby when it was hours old, breaking its leg.

Zookeepers then had to care for Cassie round the clock as they tried to mimic all interactions as closely as they could to typical chimpanzee behaviour.

Keepers have had to work around the clock caring for Cassie, trying to mimic interactions with chimp behaviour. (ABC Capricornia: Katrina Beavan)

After healing, staff attempted to re-introduce Cassie to mother Sile as well as another female adult in the troop, Mary.

But it was unsuccessful, with both females showing aggression towards Cassie, who was left with bruising and bite marks.

At the time the zoo said it would discuss possible next steps with experts in the field.

Cassie had positive reactions to the troop through mesh screens before the unsuccessful reunion. (Supplied: Rockhampton Regional Council)

In a social media video posted on Thursday morning, primate team leader Jo Thrower said Cassie had healed well from the interactions.

"From this we've had a lot of discussions within our team and with specialists from around Australasia and Europe," Ms Thrower said.

"We've concluded that Cassie needs to find a new troop to go to and become a part of."

Ms Thrower said it was very important for the young chimp's development to be around others of its kind as soon as possible.

"Staying in human care she's going to grow up believing she's a human, which will only cause bigger issues down the line when she does eventually go in with chimps," she said.

"The sooner we can get this done the better."

She conceded that the Rockhampton community already "loved" Cassie and would like to see the chimp grow up locally.

"But we need to do what's best for her welfare, and to put her back in with our troop she's only going to get hurt."

Rockhampton Zoo curator Blair Chapman nursing baby Cassie, who is receiving 24/7 care from keepers. (Supplied: Rockhampton Regional Council)

Where to next?

Ms Thrower said Cassie's development was going well and the chimp was hitting all the appropriate milestones.

The zoo did not confirm which facility Cassie would be sent to as it was "still working through options" and would update the community as soon as the final decision was made.

Cassie is the offspring of 19-year-old alpha female Sile and the troop’s alpha male, Alon. (Supplied: Rockhampton Regional Council)

The zoo is owned and funded by the Rockhampton Regional Council which has not yet responded to the ABC about the costs incurred with hand-rearing Cassie.

The young chimp was named after chimpanzee Cassius, a resident at the Rockhampton Zoo for almost 40 years, and a local woman named Cassie who donated colostrum during the initial weeks after the primate's birth.

Cassie will leave behind a seven-chimp troop with four males aged from six to 30 years old and three females aged between eight and 23.

World.title: Family of Molly Ticehurst face her killer in emotional court appearance
World.content:
The father of a murdered childcare worker has told his daughter's killer: "I hope that every night Molly's screams keep you awake."

Warning: This story contains descriptions of domestic violence and murder.

Victim impact statements from members of Molly Ticehurst's family are today being delivered in the NSW Supreme Court at Orange, some 100 kilometres east of where she was found dead in her Forbes home two years ago.

In November last year, Daniel Billings pleaded guilty to murdering his ex-girlfriend after he broke into her house late at night on April 14, 2024 and stabbed her 15 times.

Supporters of Molly Ticehurst arrive at the Supreme Court in Orange on Thursday morning. (ABC Central West: Hamish Cole)

He also admitted to killing a pet dachshund with a hammer and breaching an apprehended violence order.

Billings was out on bail at the time of her murder, a fact that sparked a nation-wide outcry over bail laws for domestic violence offenders.

Ms Ticehurst's father, Tony Ticehurst, told the court that "no sentence will ever be long enough".

"I hope that every night Molly's screams keep you awake," he said.

Tony Ticehurst (left), Molly Ticehurst's father, arriving at the Supreme Court in Orange. (ABC News: Hamish Cole)

"When she died, a part of me died with her.

"I am no longer just Tony, people look at me and say 'that's the woman who was killed's father'."

Family and domestic violence support services: NSW Domestic Violence Line on 1800 656 463

Lifeline on 131 114

Men's Referral Service on 1300 766 491

Mensline on 1300 789 978

Full Stop Australia on 1800 385 578

Emergency services on Triple Zero (000) if you need immediate care

Mr Ticehurst told the court that he would be forever proud that "Molly's Law" had been introduced in the wake of his daughter's death.

In June 2024, NSW passed a law making it mandatory for electronic monitoring devices to be worn by people who were on bail for certain DV charges.

Those accused of serious domestic violence offences must also now demonstrate why they should be given bail and court registrars are no longer allowed to make bail decisions.

"I still ask myself why it took Molly's life for this to happen," Mr Ticehurst said.

"I will grieve the loss of you for the rest of my life."

Son carries Molly's ashes with him

Ms Ticehurst's cousin, Melissa Shaw, told the court her death had "destroyed" each member of her family in their own way.

"It is heartbreaking to see Molly's only child take the urn with her ashes wherever he can," she said.

"Molly should never have been a headline.

"I never want my children to forget her … but with that comes a reminder that she will never come home."

Daniel Billings is accused of murdering Molly Ticehurst. (Supplied)

Billings arrived at the court on Thursday morning in a police van wearing a black suit with a white shirt, white trainers, and his dreadlocked hair tied back off his face.

He entered the courtroom and looked around the space, which was packed with Ms Ticehurst's family members, journalists and supporters wearing T-shirts inscribed with messages such as "#HernameisMolly".

Supporters of Ms Ticehurst were staring straight ahead while her mother cradled her head in her hand.

World.title: Man airlifted to Melbourne hospital after firebombing gone wrong
World.content:
A man has suffered critical burns in what appears to be a bungled firebombing of a shop at Melton, in Melbourne's outer-west.

Victoria Police said emergency services were called to reports of a fire in Alexander Street, Melton, shortly before 3am.

A man aged in his 20s was found at the scene with critical burns and was flown to the Alfred Hospital.

Ambulance Victoria said the man suffered upper and lower body injuries.

Several people can be seen at the scene of the fire in the early hours of Thursday morning. (Supplied)

CCTV from the scene shows a ute reversing into the building, before several men get out with what appears to be jerry cans full of fuel.

A few moments later, a ball of flame engulfs both men.

One man can be seen rolling around on the ground trying to extinguish flames before getting into the vehicle, where more flames erupt.

Fire crews were called to the scene just before 3am. (ABC News: Georgia Lenton-Williams)

Victoria Police said they are still looking for two men allegedly involved in the incident.

Police believe one of the missing men may have severe burns to his hands and feet.

Detective Inspector Chris Murray from the Arson and Explosives Squad said the incident was extremely dangerous.

"We have said repeatedly that deliberately lighting fires comes with immense risk, not only to the broader community but also to the offenders involved," he said.

A crime scene has been established and police are investigating the circumstances of the fire. (ABC News: Georgia Lenton-Williams)

"We have also seen incidents where offenders have died as a result of sustaining burns and this remains a very real possibility to happen again with this incident.

" Fire is uncontrollable and unpredictable and we can only be thankful it's not an innocent member of the public who has been injured. "

The ute used in the incident was later found on the Western Highway at Hopetoun Park, around 50 kilometres north-west of Melbourne.

Police said the circumstances were still under investigation but that it appeared to have been a targeted attack.

Police said the fire was being treated as suspicious. (ABC News: Georgia Lenton-Williams)

"If there is anyone out there who witnessed the fire or has any information at all about who is responsible, then I urge those people to come forward and tell us before this happens again with potentially fatal consequences," Detective Inspector Murray said.

Fire Rescue Victoria (FRV) said its crews were on the scene within four minutes and brought the fire under control around 3:12am.

"The incident was deemed suspicious and handed to Victoria Police for investigation," an FRV spokesperson said.

World.title: Theft of sanitary items demonstrates period poverty desperation
World.content:
Using socks as sanitary pads, wearing tampons for more than two days and stealing products from supermarkets are just some of the lengths women and girls are going to in order to afford period products.

Cate Sherlock is an Adelaide-based social worker and says it is an invisible struggle plaguing communities across the state.

"Young women entering supermarkets and stealing products for the month is a recurring thing I hear," she said.

Cate Sherlock would like to see psycho-social assessments include period product affordability. (ABC Riverland: Amelia Walters)

"They are wearing period products for a long period of time and then getting asked about their hygiene because they start to smell.

"There is stigma and shame about having poor self-care, when in reality they can't afford multiple period products in a day."

With 66 per cent of people who menstruate struggling to afford period products in SA at some point, many say the state needs to catch up and address its menstrual inequality issue.

Cate Sherlock says stealing is a recurring thing she hears from people experiencing period poverty. (ABC Riverland: Amelia Walters)

Teachers paying out of pocket

The ABC heard from five government workers, including teachers, who were witnessing period poverty first-hand.

Three spoke under the condition of anonymity due to their roles in the public sector.

"I know the year 6 teachers buy products and leave them in the drawers in their classroom so girls can access them," one SA wellbeing teacher said.

One teacher says other education budgets were often utilised to purchase sanitary products. (ABC Riverland: Amelia Walters)

"Many families are struggling to put food on the table.

"[They] are struggling to pay for such expensive products and it's going to get worse with our current climate."

A public high school teacher said social justice budgets were often utilised to purchase sanitary products.

Some teachers say they leave period products in drawers in their classroom so girls can access them. (ABC Riverland: Amelia Walters)

"My site purchases supplies from our wellbeing budget so teachers don't feel they have to, [just] to ensure students have access to a range of products if they need them," the teacher said.

A public service social worker recounted how she has been having a conversation with someone about period poverty "close to once a fortnight".

"A lot of homeless women tell me they use items such as socks rather than sanitary pads and tampons due to the cost," she said.

" I recently had a [woman] fleeing domestic violence choose between putting petrol in their car over pads or tampons so they could flee in the middle of the night. "

SA, NT and Tasmania 'failing' people

Not-for-profit organisation Share the Dignity surveyed more than 150,000 Australians who menstruate in 2024.

Of those, 66 per cent of South Australians had struggled to afford period products at some point.

Chief executive Rochelle Courtenay said period poverty was a national issue that was growing, with the charity to date donating 6.2 million packets of period products since it began in 2015.

Rochelle Courtenay says 200,000 packets of period products are only enough to last 50,000 women for four months. (ABC News: Mark Leonardi)

"When the data came out in 2024 we had 3.3 million Australians living below the poverty line," she said.

"That number has now increased to 5.5 million Australians."

Ms Courtenay said the only states and territories "failing" were Tasmania, the Northern Territory and South Australia.

"ACT is leading the way with a bill passed that makes it mandatory to provide period products in [places where] somebody is being educated, as well as hospitals, libraries and communal places," she said.

Some Australian states have period product vending machines. (ABC News: Mark Leonardi)

"In Victoria, they have just rolled out 1,400 free period product vending machines, and they provide period products [in most public spaces].

"In Queensland, period products are in every primary and secondary school, as well as WA and New South Wales."

Legislative change needed

Former South Australian Legislative Council MP Connie Bonaros put forward the Period Products and Facilities (Access) Bill in March 2025.

The proposed bill was modelled on the ACT's which came into effect in 2023.

While the bill did not pass the Lower House and Ms Bonaros is no longer acting as a member of parliament, legislative change is still what she wants to see.

"We had the opportunity to lead the way when it comes to period poverty in South Australia, now we're playing catch up," she said.

Connie Bonaros says while SA had the opportunity to lead in change, it is now playing catch-up. (ABC News: Marco Catalano)

The state government previously committed a total of $564,000 in 2023 over three years to fund free period products in some public schools.

It was an initiative Ms Bonaros said had likely only funded around 1,250 students with products.

"Victoria introduced its [period product] funding model and they threw $23 million towards a similar program rollout," she said.

Ms Bonaros said not-for-profit charities like Kickstart for Kids, of which she is an ambassador, donates more than 2,000 products a month to 200 SA public schools.

"Sadly we're a far cry from where we need to be," she said.

Teachers have purchased sanitary items out of their own pocket for their students. (ABC News: Mark Leonardi)

Minister for Education Lucy Hood declined an interview, and a department spokesperson did not confirm whether legislative reforms would be considered in the future.

In a statement the department said it currently provided period products to more than 500 public schools.

"This program will continue in our schools, supporting around 50,000 students each year," the statement read.

"All South Australian public schools with year 5 and above enrolments receive funding to provide period products, with additional support directed to schools experiencing greater disadvantage."

It is a reality Connie Bonaros said needed to change.

World.title: Medvedev puts bird disruption aside to claim win at US Open
World.content:
Daniil Medvedev overcame an unusual interruption from two birds to fly into the third round of the US Open as he flattened American wildcard Sebastian Gorzny 6-1 6-3 7-5 at Louis Armstrong Stadium on Wednesday, local time.

The 2021 champion fired off 14 aces in a lopsided affair, where a mid-match avian distraction served up an odd bit of drama. Medvedev next plays either Spain's Jaume Munar or Frenchman Arthur Rinderknech.

"Being on the court, I was happy with my level," the Russian said.

"I love this court and I love you guys."

The Russian broke his opponent from the baseline in the opening game and needed only 21 minutes to get through the first set, firing off 10 winners to just two from Gorzny, who was outmatched in only his second major main draw match.

Medvedev has kept a calm demeanour in New York — in contrast to his dramatic first-round exit last year — but had his patience tested when a pair of birds appeared on the net during a rally midway through the second set, prompting the umpire to replay the point.

"I saw them straight away and thought the point would stop straight away," said Medvedev, who estimated that they continued to play for 45 seconds before the umpire intervened.

"The moment I hit the winner, we stop, and I say, 'Why?'"

Daniil Medvedev was unhappy that the umpire paused the game. (Reuters: Shannon Stapleton)

He got over it pretty quickly, keeping the demolition job going in the third set, where he briefly sniped at the chair umpire, calling him "crazy," during the changeover after the third game and survived a 33-shot rally in the sixth.

Gorzny improved his level in the third set, saving four break points in the ninth game, but it was too little too late as Medvedev harnessed his powerful forehand to break the American in the 11th game and sealed it with an unreturnable serve.

The bird incident joined a growing list of odd moments in Flushing Meadows for Medvedev, who has endured a love-hate relationship with the New York crowd since his memorable turn as pantomime villain in 2019.

He overcame a booing crowd to beat Spaniard Feliciano Lopez en route to the final that year, losing to Rafa Nadal in the championship match but earning the fans' begrudging respect.

"This would definitely be in the top five [unusual moments]," Medvedev told reporters.

"It's OK. It happens."

Reuters

World.title: 'Complicated' relationship between ex-shock jocks probed at Jones's trial
World.content:
Former radio host Ray Hadley has told the trial of his 2GB rival Alan Jones that the broadcaster targeted him for disloyalty after he signed a secret contract to take over the breakfast show.

Mr Hadley has wrapped up his evidence in Mr Jones's criminal trial, where he has pleaded not guilty to 22 counts of indecent assault and sexual touching of six men.

The former 2GB morning show host has been accused by Mr Jones's defence team of trying to "destroy" their client by colluding with one of the alleged victims, Complainant C, to bring down Mr Jones with a criminal complaint.

Mr Hadley agreed in the NSW Local Court on Thursday that he had "animosity" for Mr Jones in late 2019.

But he said Mr Jones had been targeting him before then.

"I'd been targeted by Mr Jones when he found out that I'd signed a contract to take his position, even though I never took his position," he said.

" He was targeting me because he thought I was disloyal. "

Mr Jones denies all allegations against him. (ABC News: Abubakr Sajid)

On Wednesday the court heard Mr Hadley signed a $4 million contract in late 2018 to take on the breakfast role in mid-2019, because one of the station's shareholders was concerned Mr Jones was costing him too much money in defamation cases.

Mr Hadley said after that, Mr Jones tried to "dig up dirt" on him and tried to frame him for a workplace assault that never happened.

"Anything they could to white ant me, white ant my program, just generally make life more difficult for me," he said on Thursday.

He was also asked to explain why he said "this bloke needs to be destroyed" in reference to Mr Jones, in a text message to Complainant C.

"It was in reference to the proceedings we're here about at the moment," Mr Hadley said. "I said I'd stick by him [Complainant C] and I'd support him in every way no matter what course of action he decided to take and that's why I'm here today."

Defence barrister Gabrielle Bashir SC put to Mr Hadley that he had not told the truth about a conversation with Complainant C in 2019, where he alleged the man confided in him that Mr Jones had assaulted him more than 10 years earlier.

Mr Hadley said he rejected that entirely.

'Very complicated' working relationship

In re-examination by the crown, Mr Hadley was also taken to a more cordial text message exchange with Mr Jones, where he thanked his colleague for some well wishes.

"Our relationship was very complicated," Mr Hadley told the court.

"We went from being very close to very distant.

"Much of my success as a broadcaster was due to him.

"He was gracious, I returned it. I was appreciative of what he did for me as a broadcaster.

"We had stand up brawls … he said he'd never work with me again.

"He wanted me out of the building.

"We were both under tremendous pressure constantly to deliver and as a result it was a tumultuous relationships, sometimes warm and friendly and sometimes hostile."

Mr Hadley describes his relationship with Mr Jones as "tumultuous". (ABC News: Abubakr Sajid)

Mr Hadley was dismissed after finishing his evidence, and made brief comments to reporters outside court, saying he "can't say anything until the matter has been totally and utterly dealt with."

Allegations concerning Mr Jones were first published by Sydney Morning Herald (SMH) investigative journalist Kate McClymont in December 2023.

The court on Wednesday heard Mr Hadley described the article as being "50 years in the making" in a text message to Complainant C.

"That c*** will be in the foetal position when he reads the story in the morning," he said in the message.

Mr Hadley denied suggestions he had a vested interest in the outcome of Mr Jones's case.

He also rejected the suggestion that he pushed Complainant C to make his allegations in a bid to have Mr Jones dropped from the breakfast program.

Mr Jones's trial is now in its fourth week. The trial continues.

World.title: LA Clippers fined $40m over 'flagrant' rules breaches
World.content:
The NBA has imposed a sweeping punishment against the Los Angeles Clippers for violating salary cap circumvention rules, suspending owner Steve Ballmer for one year, fining the team $US30 million ($41.5 million) and forcing it to forfeit five draft picks.

Two-time NBA Finals MVP Kawhi Leonard was also hit with a $US700,000 ($977,000) penalty, president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank was banned for six months and team president of business operations Gillian Zucker was suspended for one year.

The league came down hard on the organisation on Wednesday after a nearly year-long investigation led by an outside law firm.

The Clippers had said multiple times that they had done nothing wrong and expected to be exonerated.

"I think that we're going to be in the clear," Leonard said in April, "so I'm not stressing it."

At the same time, Frank said: "If you know Steve and know Steve's integrity, you know there's nothing to it. We believe and we've very confident we're on the right side of this."

The team maintained that stance on Wednesday.

Steve Ballmer (left) will sit out the next 12 months as part of his punishment for the breaches. (Getty Images: Katelyn Mulcahy)

"We vehemently reject the NBA's findings, which are the result of a heavily biased investigation seeking to justify a predetermined narrative rather than facts and evidence," the team said in a statement.

"What the league told us privately differs from what it announced today publicly, and they have not held themselves close to the standard Commissioner [Adam] Silver set at the start of this investigation to ensure its fairness and accuracy."

The Clippers said they will "now fight just as hard to demonstrate our innocence. We intend to vigorously challenge these findings and penalties through every avenue available to us and look forward to an ethical and impartial arbitration process."

The league said it and the players' union agreed to confirm the penalties as final and binding on all parties. It said the outside law firm continued to receive information involving the investigation, and the league "will consider further action as appropriate".

"I am deeply disappointed by the flagrant violations of our rules and by the Clippers' institutional and leadership failures that led to this misconduct," Silver said in a statement.

"The severity of the penalties reflects the seriousness of the violations."

Adam Silver says he is "deeply disappointed" in the Clippers' breaches. (Getty Images: Elsa)

The NBA began investigating in September 2025 whether a $28 million endorsement contract between Leonard and Aspiration Fund Adviser LLC — a company that filed for bankruptcy last year — broke league rules, following a report by journalist Pablo Torre.

Earlier this year, Aspiration co-founder Joseph Sanberg was sentenced to 14 years in federal prison after pleading guilty to defrauding investors and lenders of at least $248 million.

The Clippers released a letter from Ballmer's attorney David Kelley to Silver, in which he described the investigation as "a witch hunt" and the subsequent penalties as a "gross injustice".

Kelley accused Silver of not keeping his promises that the investigation would be governed by due process and fundamental fairness, as well as the burden being on the league to prove any violations through evidence.

"League counsel has acknowledged in our discussions that the league does not believe there was an agreement between the Clippers and Aspiration to funnel money to Kawhi Leonard. League counsel also agreed with the Department of Justice, the Securities and Exchange Commission, and a federal judge that Mr. Ballmer was a victim of Joe Sanberg's fraud — not a participant," wrote Kelley, a partner in the firm O'Melveny and Myers.

"Mr Ballmer's reputation has been irreparably damaged as he now finds himself embroiled not only in this heavily biased investigation, but in civil litigation, the Aspiration bankruptcy proceeding, and more," Kelley wrote.

Kelley wrote that no league rule prohibits team personnel from making introductions to both sponsors and vendors in response to player requests.

"Retroactively punishing the Clippers for violating a rule that never existed is hardly consistent with due process," Kelley wrote.

The league said Ballmer knowingly sought to help Leonard obtain off-court income deals, approved a business deal that he knew was a precondition for Aspiration to enter into an endorsement contract with Leonard, and for failing to create conditions under which his team followed league rules.

"I accept full responsibility for lapses in judgement by people within my inner circle and regret the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family," Leonard said in a statement issued through his new agent, Harrison Gaines.

The NBA said Leonard, through his former business manager and uncle Dennis Robertson, "violated the circumvention rules by pressuring the Clippers to assist him in obtaining off-court income opportunities, successfully obtaining those opportunities, and failing to reimburse payments by the Clippers for personal expenses."

"I entered into my contract with the Clippers as well as the agreements in question in good faith, fully committed to fulfilling my obligations and with no knowledge of any intent on anyone's part to circumvent the salary cap," Leonard said in his statement.

The league said Ballmer was suspended for "knowingly seeking to help Mr Leonard obtain off-court income opportunities," among other issues.

Kawhi Leonard is set to return to Toronto for the upcoming season. (Getty Images: Patrick McDermott)

Leonard's trade to the Toronto Raptors has been on hold pending the outcome of the investigation. The Raptors had said they still want Leonard, and he apparently is just as eager to return to the team where he won an NBA title and was Finals MVP in 2019.

"As I return to Toronto, I am focused on what I can control, closing this chapter, and moving forward with a clean slate," Leonard said in his statement.

The Clippers and their personnel will be under a compliance and monitoring program by the league for five years and Robertson was banned from doing business with NBA teams for five years.

The league penalised Frank for his involvement with the impermissible endorsement arrangements and for approving impermissible expenses incurred by Leonard and his family.

Zucker was banned for being primarily and directly culpable for the illegal endorsement arrangements and for lying to investigators. Both will lose their salaries during their bans.

It is not the first time the Clippers have run afoul of NBA rules under Ballmer, who bought the team for $2 billion in August 2014.

They were fined $250,000 a year later for violating rules against offering unauthorised business or investment opportunities to players during their courting of free agent DeAndre Jordan. A presentation to him improperly included a $200,000-per-year deal with luxury car maker Lexus.

Ballmer, 70, was CEO of Microsoft from 2000 to 2014.

World.title: Australia news LIVE: More than 1200 dead in Nepal, Tibet as 38 Australians remain unaccounted for; Chalmers concedes Labor’s role in falling house values
World.content:
As the search for 38 missing Australians in Nepal and Tibet enters its second week, Wong says the government is hopeful, but concern for the missing is growing.

“We all hold on to hope, and we’ve got to hold on to hope. I’ve also said we have great concerns for the Australians who remain accounted for, and those concerns deepen every day, every hour, that they remain unaccounted for,” she said.

“I can indicate to you that we have dedicated case officers assigned to next of kin, and we are also working closely with the Australian Federal Police to provide support to next of kin.”

World.title: The ‘miracle house’ that survived Nepal’s floods
World.content:
WorldAsiaNepal The ‘miracle house’ that survived Nepal’s floods Mujib Mashal and Binod Ghimire September 3, 2026 — 11:42am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Dhunge Bazaar, Nepal: For some, it has become known as the “miracle” green house. For others arriving to stare in wonderment and take selfies, it is simply “the viral house”. When a ferocious torrent of water, mud and debris swept away everything in its path in Nepal last week, it created a whirlpool of destruction around the Pyakurel family home in Dhunge Bazaar. A video that spread far and wide on social media showed the family helplessly looking down from their third-floor balcony at the angry waves, barely fluid, threatening to overwhelm them. Loading But the house stood firm. Chhatra Bahadur Pyakurel, 67, had just returned from taking his grandson to the school bus when the floods – caused by a massive glacier collapse in the Himalayan region between Nepal and Tibet – reached their home.



For more than an hour, the family could only watch the carnage around them – first from the balcony, and then having climbed to the roof, as the wall of water and debris grew deeper and wilder. “At first we did not know what would happen or whether we would survive,” Pyakurel said. “But after some time, we realised there was nothing more we could do. Our lives were in the hands of the almighty God, whether he would save us or let us drown.” “The only thought that kept troubling me was about my grandson, who had already left for school. I kept thinking: ‘If we all die, who will look after him?’” A view of the green house in Dhunge after the floodwater subsided. X Online images of the house – still standing, alone amid a wasteland of mud and debris – went viral. Days after the devastation, as the road in front of the house was partially reopened and traffic slowly returned to Dhunge Bazaar, visitors climbed the ridge for a view of the house and river, now calmer, its flow still muddy.



The house has its own pinpoint on Google Maps as a “flood-proof” attraction. Related Article Floods This valley was the last known location of a Sydney family. Then a wave 100 metres high hit Pillars and walls of the first two storeys remain. On the third-storey balcony, the washing machine remained, along with a pile of laundry. The roof – with its water tanks, a solar water heater, a small family temple and many tall plants – looked neatly intact. The house has become one of the rare stories of survival amid a grim picture of devastation, the extent of which grows daily. The death toll in Nepal exceeds 1200, with almost 4000 more people still missing, and hundreds more remaining unaccounted for in Tibet. Nepalese Army soldiers survey the devastation in Dhunge. KATE GERAGHTY



Missions complicated by continuous rain –and entire towns covered in the kind of soft mud that makes helicopter landings difficult – have rescued more than 11,000 people. Thousands of whom are in temporary shelters. In the surrounding Nuwakot district alone, at least 1200 homes have been destroyed and more than 1000 others partially damaged. Related Article Analysis

Floods China’s flood rescue is a no-go zone for foreign media. What does it have to hide? Communications remain a major issue in a country with difficult terrain. Dozens of bridges have been wiped out and stretches of road, including the one just beyond Dhunge Bazaar, destroyed. Bishu Mani Rimal, 45, who was among the crowd staring at the surviving house, lives 4.8 kilometres downstream, where the torrent of water had slowed slightly.



“Who would believe people in that situation would survive?” he said. “I thought they didn’t even have a 1 per cent chance.” Surveying the destruction, he said that power turbines on the other side of the river were gone. So, too, was an entire bazaar. Four homes owned by the same extended family had also vanished. “One house was so new, they hadn’t even moved in,” he said. Pyakurel, the patriarch, said the ground floor of the green house was built in 1995 when he had a grocery store. As his business expanded, including selling liquor wholesale, the family added floors.



He said that after the family spent an hour trapped on the roof, the flow receded and neighbours came to help, using metal pipes to create a makeshift ladder to safety. He said the house may have remained standing because its pillars were anchored by drilling deep into the rock, but he also said that it was spared by God. Theories about the house have cropped up, with some saying that a ridge jutting out into the path of the torrent had helped shield it. Related Article Live

National News Live Australia news LIVE: More than 1200 dead in Nepal, Tibet as 38 Australians remain unaccounted for; Chalmers concedes Labor’s role in falling house values As he was still assessing the damage, Pyakurel had temporarily relocated to Kathmandu, the capital. But he feared that on the first two floors, “everything is gone. Even our family’s most important documents, including citizenship certificates, passports and land registration certificates, were destroyed.” But he was grateful that his grandson was safe, as the school was on higher ground. The family reunited the day after the flood.

World.title: Alan Jones trial live updates: Ray Hadley to return for further cross-examination as indecent assault, sexual touching trial continues
World.content:
Warning: Graphic content

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Alan Jones’ criminal trial in the Downing Centre Local Court in Sydney. I will be keeping you informed of the latest developments with my colleagues Clare Sibthorpe and Harriet Alexander.

Jones, 85, is standing trial on 20 counts of indecent assault and two counts of sexual touching without consent spanning six male complainants and a 17-year period from 2003 to 2020. The former 2GB broadcaster denies any of the alleged physical acts occurred.

Ray Hadley and Alan Jones outside the Downing Centre Local Court on Wednesday. Dominic Lorrimer

Jones’ long-time colleague at 2GB, Ray Hadley, returns to the witness box today for further cross-examination by Jones’ barrister, Gabrielle Bashir, SC.

Hadley has given evidence that complainant “C”, one of the six men who has accused Jones of unwanted touching and kissing, confided in him in late 2019 about the alleged indecent assaults.

Bashir has foreshadowed she will argue Hadley encouraged “C” to make the allegations because he coveted Jones’ breakfast radio slot. Hadley has described that argument as “completely wrong and misinformed”.

During cross-examination on Wednesday, Hadley was shown a series of explosive text messages he sent “C” about Jones, including one in December 2023 before this masthead published an article by chief investigative reporter Kate McClymont revealing the complainant’s allegations against Jones. “That c--- will be in the foetal position when he reads the story in the morning,” Hadley wrote. “It’s been 50 years in the making.”

In another message to “C” that month, Hadley said: “The low c--- ...[he’s] not just taking on victims, he’s taking on me and Kate. I won’t rest until we bury him, figuratively speaking or literally.” Asked if the “we” was him and the complainant, Hadley said: “I think it was probably me and Kate McClymont”.

Hadley also texted “C” about Jones in 2019: “This bloke needs to be destroyed.”

Hadley revealed during his cross-examination that he signed a “secret contract” in late 2018 to take over Jones’ breakfast radio slot at 2GB from July 2019. He denied he coveted the slot and said the lure was financial.

The deal fell over, but he insisted 2GB honour the agreement to double his salary to $4 million.

He denied it was a difficult time for him when Jones re-signed his contract for two years in May 2019, saying: “Inadvertently Mr Jones had doubled my salary for doing the same job.”

Hadley told the court that a 2GB employee told him in about 2019 that Alan Jones had “marshalled the troops and said, ‘dig up some dirt on Hadley’.”

In an unusual development, Hadley admitted he winked at a person in the public gallery during his evidence. He told the court he had mistakenly believed it was a reporter at the Herald he didn’t know who had “called me … I think ‘scruffy’” in a news article. This masthead did not use that word in its reporting but had referred to Hadley speaking “gruffly”.

Judge Glenn Walsh ordered an investigation by the sheriff into any phone contact between Hadley and any journalist yesterday about his evidence. No Herald journalist covering the trial has had contact with Hadley during his evidence.

Support is available from the National Sexual Assault, Domestic Family Violence Counselling Service at 1800RESPECT (1800 737 732) or the Men’s Referral Service on 1300 766 491.

World.title: ASX edges higher as Wall Street climbs; Corporate Travel plummets
World.content:
Updated BusinessMarketsWorld markets ASX edges higher as Wall Street climbs; Corporate Travel plummets Staff writers Updated September 3, 2026 — 11:22am ,first published September 3, 2026 — 5:14am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

The Australian sharemarket has inched higher at the open after stocks rose on Wall Street overnight as gains by big technology companies and relatively steady oil prices and bond yields helped boost the market after a downbeat start to the week. The S&P/ASX 200 was up 12.4 points, or 0.1 per cent, in early trade to 8990.8. The ASX lost 1 per cent on Wednesday. The Australian dollar is stronger at US71.71¢. Wall Street climbed as oil prices and bond yields steadied. AP Shares of Corporate Travel Management plunged more than 80 per cent to a low of $2.81 after the recommenced trading, more than a year after the discovery of significant overcharging and accounting errors in its UK/Europe operations. This week the company finally released audited financial statements for the 2025 and 2026 financial years. The 2026 accounts for the year ending June 30 received a qualified opinion from its auditors and reported a net profit of $17.7 million, compared to a loss of $348.5 million in the previous year due to significant writedowns.



Mining stocks are largely stronger, with Fortescue up 2.1 per cent and Rio Tinto 1.3 per cent stronger. BHP was down 2.1 per cent as it traded ex-dividend. Gold miners advanced, with the price of the precious metal holding a gain to trade at about $US4385 an ounce as US President Donald Trump appeared to rule out prolonged military action in the Middle East, easing inflationary concerns of a renewed spike in energy prices. Northern Star and Evolution Mining added 1.6 per cent in early trade. Financial stocks are higher with ANZ Bank leading the way with a 1.1 per cent gain. Commonwealth Bank inched up 0.1 per cent, National Australia Bank added 0.5 per cent and Westpac was 0.6 per cent higher in early trade. Energy stocks slid as oil prices dipped overnight. Brent, the international standard, was down 0.4 per cent in early Asian trade to $US95.26 a barrel. Woodside Energy lost 3 per cent as it traded ex-dividend while Santos slipped 0.3 per cent. Among the refiners, Ampol shed 0.7 per cent and Viva Energy lost 0.5 per cent. Brent crude settled up 1 per cent at $US95.63. Chevron edged 0.3 per cent higher after confirming it would expand operations in Venezuela. Technology stocks slid lower as Xero lost 0.1 per cent, WiseTech fell 1.4 per cent, Technology One lost 1.8 per cent and NEXTDC dropped 0.4 per cent. Life360 was 2.6 per cent higher.



Wall Street has been under pressure this week from rising oil prices and a bond-market sell-off. The rocky start to September follows a mostly positive August during which every major index notched a gain for the month. It remains gripped by anxiety over rising prices, government debt and the impact of global conflicts on the US and the global economy. Overnight on Wall Street, technology and communication services stocks accounted for some of the strongest gains. Computer memory seller Micron Technology gained 2.4 per cent. Chipmaker Nvidia, whose big market value tend to give it more influence over the broader market’s direction, rose 3.2 per cent, lifting the Dow Jones Industrial Average by 0.6 per cent. The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq composite both gained 0.5 per cent. Meta added 2.5 per cent as it released its most powerful artificial intelligence model yet, with its chief AI officer saying its capabilities are edging closer to top competitors. Developers can now access and pay for Muse Spark 1.3, an updated version of its most advanced model, the company said. It will soon roll out the update to users of Meta’s social media platforms, like Instagram and Facebook, as well as Meta AI. “This is our biggest jump so far on model performance,” Meta’s chief AI officer Alexandr Wang said in an interview on Wednesday, pointing to advancements in the model’s coding and agentic capabilities (requiring limited supervision to complete tasks on behalf of human users). Wang said the update put Meta on par with recently released AI models from its rivals OpenAI and Anthropic.



Dell Technologies jumped 15.8 per cent for the biggest gain among S&P 500 stocks after delivering strong second-quarter profits amid accelerating demand for artificial intelligence computing. The company also raised its fiscal year revenue outlook. Palo Alto Networks also reported quarterly results that topped Wall Street’s expectations, citing a strong market for AI cybersecurity, but its shares fell 9.3 per cent. Meanwhile, banks and credit card issuers also helped boost the market. Capital One Financial rose 2.5 per cent and American Express added 1.8 per cent. Markets in Europe fell after markets in Asia closed lower. The big focus this week will be the government’s broader employment report for August, which will be released on Friday. The previous report for July showed that the jobs market stalled, with employers cutting positions.



Related Article Opinion

Oil Trump kidnapped Venezuela’s president. Now he’s hijacking its future Stephen Bartholomeusz Senior business columnist Both inflation and the job market have been key focuses for Wall Street and the Federal Reserve. “Friday’s employment report, and perhaps even more importantly next week’s inflation data, will play a significant role in determining whether policymakers decide to raise rates in September,” said Angelo Kourkafas, senior global strategist, investment strategy at Edward Jones, in a research note. The Fed is trying to balance its task of supporting employment and taming inflation. Wall Street expects the central bank to raise interest rates before the year ends in an effort to cool inflation, which remains well above 3 per cent. The Fed has a stated goal of cooling inflation to 2 per cent. The bond market has been selling off, which is a signal that it expects borrowing costs to rise.



The yield on the 10-year Treasury, which tends to impact mortgage rates, rose to 4.80 per cent from 4.79 per cent late on Tuesday. It has been rising steadily throughout the year and was as low as 4.20 per cent at the beginning of 2026. The yield on the two-year Treasury, which closely tracks expectations for Federal Reserve moves on interest rates, held steady at 4.39 per cent. It is significantly higher for the year, though, and was as low as 3.50 per cent at the beginning of 2026. Investors are also betting on a 64 per cent chance that the Fed will raise rates at its upcoming meeting in September, according to CME FedWatch. With AP, Bloomberg The Market Recap newsletter is a wrap of the day’s trading. Get it each weekday afternoon.

World.title: The moment a man is struck by lightning – then walks away unharmed
World.content:
WorldNorth AmericaExtreme weather The moment a man is struck by lightning – then walks away unharmed Alexandra Snow September 3, 2026 — 11:11am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

When Thomas Fahmy stepped out his front door in New York’s Staten Island to head to the dentist, he was hit with a bolt from above. Footage from a home security camera shows the US Republican Party political staffer suddenly drop to the ground in a fiery flash – just metres from his car. “I didn’t even have a chance to step back, I just fell to the floor,” he said of the shock incident on August 27. Fahmy suffered no severe injuries and remained conscious the entire time, only reporting an intense burning sensation, tingling and pain in both of his feet.



Seconds later, he gathered himself, stood up and hobbled away, knocking on the nearest door for help. Stephanie Homan came to the front door with a young child in her arms, which Fahmy said reminded him of an image of the Madonna and child. Stephanie Homan came to the front door with a young child in her arms, which Fahmy said reminded him of an image of the Madonna and child. This image of Madonna and Christ Child is in St. Peter’s Basilica at the Vatican. AP Homan helped him inside her home, called 911 and within minutes emergency responders arrived. Fahmy was taken to Northwell Staten Island University Hospital, in Ocean Breeze, to be examined by doctors.



He did not suffer any visible burns from the lightning strike but was monitored overnight before being released the following day. After being discharged, he bought a Mega Millions lottery ticket and then attended church, where that day’s Bible reading was about the apocalypse, which he thought was particularly apt. The odds of winning the Mega Millions lottery jackpot are one in 300 million. Representative Nicole Malliotakis, a Republican from New York. Bloomberg Fahmy works in US representative Nicole Malliotakis’ Staten Island office. Malliotakis said: “We are grateful that Thomas, a member of my congressional staff, is alive and well after being struck by lightning last week.



“I thank the good Samaritan who ran to his aid and the medical staff at Staten Island University Hospital who treated him.” Fahmy gained a new perspective on life after finding himself on the ground following the lightning strike. He said: “In politics, you kind of forget sometimes that there’s something bigger than you. There is a power greater than you. “It all goes down the drain once you see life literally flash in front of your eyes.” In the US, there is roughly a one in 1.2 million chance of being struck by lightning in any given year.



While almost 90 per cent of all people struck by lightning survive, many are left with various degrees of disability, according to the US National Weather Service. Telegraph, London Get a note directly from our foreign correspondents on what’s making headlines around the world.

World.title: Rawiller confident he can get timing right again with Lindermann
World.content:
SportRacingHorse racing Rawiller confident he can get timing right again with Lindermann Craig Kerry September 3, 2026 — 11:07am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

It comes a week later than expected, but Nash Rawiller believes his return aboard Lindermann could prove perfect timing as he chases a bonus win in the group 2 Chelmsford Stakes (1600m) on Saturday at Randwick. Rawiller was to ride Godolphin star Beiwacht in the group 1 Winx Stakes at Randwick two weeks ago, with hopes Chris Waller-trained stablemate Lindermann would be scratched and saved for him to partner in the Memsie Stakes a week later at Caulfield. Nash Rawiller pushes Lindermann to victory in the Chelmsford Stakes last year. Getty Images A slight temperature for Beiwacht forced a late change, putting Rawiller on Aeliana in the Winx and back to Beiwacht instead for the group 1 Memsie, which the pair then dominated with a front-running, three-length victory. Seven-year-old Lindermann faded when first up in the Winx Stakes to finish more than seven lengths ninth. It was a similar effort to his 2025 run when 10th, and Rawiller hopes history can repeat in the Chelmsford, which they claimed with a gritty performance out front to hold off Sir Delius. Rawiller has won five times on the Lonhro gelding and they were second, ahead of Autumn Glow, in Sir Delius’ Queen Elizabeth Stakes victory last time together.



Rawiller was forgiving of Lindermann’s Winx run and keen to get him back on track. He was a $2.70 TAB favourite. “He always seems to improve a lot into his second run and we’ve probably worked that over the last few seasons,” Rawiller said. “Sometimes you leave the race scratching your head a bit first-up, but then he comes out and blows them away second-up. “I thought there was a fair bit of pressure on in that race the other day, way too much pressure the first half of the race, so hopefully we can just get him into his normal rhythm and let him do his thing. “He went out after the leader a long way from home the other day, which he probably didn’t need to do.”



Nash Rawiller returns a winner on Lindermann in the Hill Stakes. Getty Images Rawiller, meanwhile, was excited about Beiwacht potentially heading to the $20 million Everest (1200m) and $10 million Golden Eagle (1500m). Godolphin Australia boss Andy Makiv has said the Manikato Stakes could be next for the three-time group 1 winner before possibly going to Australia’s two richest races. “I think with the Everest, being a strong 1400m horse, it could be an advantage, so it will be interesting,” Rawiller said. “If he can keep his confidence up and show he’s ready to go there, I think he would be one of the main chances.” Rawiller was also confident about his chances with another warhorse on Saturday, Private Eye ($3.90), in the group 2 Tramway Stakes (1400m) after the nine-year-old was strong to the line when second to Cosmic Crusader in the PB Lawrence Stakes (1400m).



Nash Rawiller winning the PB Lawrence Stakes last year on Private Eye. Getty Images “He got beat by the favourite in the Memsie, which ran so well before that, and I was really happy with his run,” he said. Rawiller has picked up the ride on Screen Icon ($21) in the Furious Stakes, and he will chase back-to-back Highway wins on Mrs Goldberg ($4.20). “I think it’s important for [Screen Icon] not to work too hard early and leave her with a good kick at the 300,” he said. “Mrs Goldberg looks well weighted again and she enjoyed sitting off that hot tempo last time. She was pretty explosive.”

World.title: The ‘miracle house’ that survived Nepal’s floods
World.content:
WorldAsiaNepal The ‘miracle house’ that survived Nepal’s floods Mujib Mashal and Binod Ghimire September 3, 2026 — 11:42am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Dhunge Bazaar, Nepal: For some, it has become known as the “miracle” green house. For others arriving to stare in wonderment and take selfies, it is simply “the viral house”. When a ferocious torrent of water, mud and debris swept away everything in its path in Nepal last week, it created a whirlpool of destruction around the Pyakurel family home in Dhunge Bazaar. A video that spread far and wide on social media showed the family helplessly looking down from their third-floor balcony at the angry waves, barely fluid, threatening to overwhelm them. Loading But the house stood firm. Chhatra Bahadur Pyakurel, 67, had just returned from taking his grandson to the school bus when the floods – caused by a massive glacier collapse in the Himalayan region between Nepal and Tibet – reached their home.



For more than an hour, the family could only watch the carnage around them – first from the balcony, and then having climbed to the roof, as the wall of water and debris grew deeper and wilder. “At first we did not know what would happen or whether we would survive,” Pyakurel said. “But after some time, we realised there was nothing more we could do. Our lives were in the hands of the almighty God, whether he would save us or let us drown.” “The only thought that kept troubling me was about my grandson, who had already left for school. I kept thinking: ‘If we all die, who will look after him?’” A view of the green house in Dhunge after the floodwater subsided. X Online images of the house – still standing, alone amid a wasteland of mud and debris – went viral. Days after the devastation, as the road in front of the house was partially reopened and traffic slowly returned to Dhunge Bazaar, visitors climbed the ridge for a view of the house and river, now calmer, its flow still muddy.



The house has its own pinpoint on Google Maps as a “flood-proof” attraction. Related Article Floods This valley was the last known location of a Sydney family. Then a wave 100 metres high hit Pillars and walls of the first two storeys remain. On the third-storey balcony, the washing machine remained, along with a pile of laundry. The roof – with its water tanks, a solar water heater, a small family temple and many tall plants – looked neatly intact. The house has become one of the rare stories of survival amid a grim picture of devastation, the extent of which grows daily. The death toll in Nepal exceeds 1200, with almost 4000 more people still missing, and hundreds more remaining unaccounted for in Tibet. Nepalese Army soldiers survey the devastation in Dhunge. KATE GERAGHTY



Missions complicated by continuous rain –and entire towns covered in the kind of soft mud that makes helicopter landings difficult – have rescued more than 11,000 people. Thousands of whom are in temporary shelters. In the surrounding Nuwakot district alone, at least 1200 homes have been destroyed and more than 1000 others partially damaged. Related Article Analysis

Floods China’s flood rescue is a no-go zone for foreign media. What does it have to hide? Communications remain a major issue in a country with difficult terrain. Dozens of bridges have been wiped out and stretches of road, including the one just beyond Dhunge Bazaar, destroyed. Bishu Mani Rimal, 45, who was among the crowd staring at the surviving house, lives 4.8 kilometres downstream, where the torrent of water had slowed slightly.



“Who would believe people in that situation would survive?” he said. “I thought they didn’t even have a 1 per cent chance.” Surveying the destruction, he said that power turbines on the other side of the river were gone. So, too, was an entire bazaar. Four homes owned by the same extended family had also vanished. “One house was so new, they hadn’t even moved in,” he said. Pyakurel, the patriarch, said the ground floor of the green house was built in 1995 when he had a grocery store. As his business expanded, including selling liquor wholesale, the family added floors.



He said that after the family spent an hour trapped on the roof, the flow receded and neighbours came to help, using metal pipes to create a makeshift ladder to safety. He said the house may have remained standing because its pillars were anchored by drilling deep into the rock, but he also said that it was spared by God. Theories about the house have cropped up, with some saying that a ridge jutting out into the path of the torrent had helped shield it. Related Article Live

National News Live Australia news LIVE: More than 1200 dead in Nepal, Tibet as 38 Australians remain unaccounted for; Chalmers concedes Labor’s role in falling house values As he was still assessing the damage, Pyakurel had temporarily relocated to Kathmandu, the capital. But he feared that on the first two floors, “everything is gone. Even our family’s most important documents, including citizenship certificates, passports and land registration certificates, were destroyed.” But he was grateful that his grandson was safe, as the school was on higher ground. The family reunited the day after the flood.

World.title: Alan Jones trial live updates: Ray Hadley to return for further cross-examination as indecent assault, sexual touching trial continues
World.content:
Warning: Graphic content

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Alan Jones’ criminal trial in the Downing Centre Local Court in Sydney. I will be keeping you informed of the latest developments with my colleagues Clare Sibthorpe and Harriet Alexander.

Jones, 85, is standing trial on 20 counts of indecent assault and two counts of sexual touching without consent spanning six male complainants and a 17-year period from 2003 to 2020. The former 2GB broadcaster denies any of the alleged physical acts occurred.

Ray Hadley and Alan Jones outside the Downing Centre Local Court on Wednesday. Dominic Lorrimer

Jones’ long-time colleague at 2GB, Ray Hadley, returns to the witness box today for further cross-examination by Jones’ barrister, Gabrielle Bashir, SC.

Hadley has given evidence that complainant “C”, one of the six men who has accused Jones of unwanted touching and kissing, confided in him in late 2019 about the alleged indecent assaults.

Bashir has foreshadowed she will argue Hadley encouraged “C” to make the allegations because he coveted Jones’ breakfast radio slot. Hadley has described that argument as “completely wrong and misinformed”.

During cross-examination on Wednesday, Hadley was shown a series of explosive text messages he sent “C” about Jones, including one in December 2023 before this masthead published an article by chief investigative reporter Kate McClymont revealing the complainant’s allegations against Jones. “That c--- will be in the foetal position when he reads the story in the morning,” Hadley wrote. “It’s been 50 years in the making.”

In another message to “C” that month, Hadley said: “The low c--- ...[he’s] not just taking on victims, he’s taking on me and Kate. I won’t rest until we bury him, figuratively speaking or literally.” Asked if the “we” was him and the complainant, Hadley said: “I think it was probably me and Kate McClymont”.

Hadley also texted “C” about Jones in 2019: “This bloke needs to be destroyed.”

Hadley revealed during his cross-examination that he signed a “secret contract” in late 2018 to take over Jones’ breakfast radio slot at 2GB from July 2019. He denied he coveted the slot and said the lure was financial.

The deal fell over, but he insisted 2GB honour the agreement to double his salary to $4 million.

He denied it was a difficult time for him when Jones re-signed his contract for two years in May 2019, saying: “Inadvertently Mr Jones had doubled my salary for doing the same job.”

Hadley told the court that a 2GB employee told him in about 2019 that Alan Jones had “marshalled the troops and said, ‘dig up some dirt on Hadley’.”

In an unusual development, Hadley admitted he winked at a person in the public gallery during his evidence. He told the court he had mistakenly believed it was a reporter at the Herald he didn’t know who had “called me … I think ‘scruffy’” in a news article. This masthead did not use that word in its reporting but had referred to Hadley speaking “gruffly”.

Judge Glenn Walsh ordered an investigation by the sheriff into any phone contact between Hadley and any journalist yesterday about his evidence. No Herald journalist covering the trial has had contact with Hadley during his evidence.

Support is available from the National Sexual Assault, Domestic Family Violence Counselling Service at 1800RESPECT (1800 737 732) or the Men’s Referral Service on 1300 766 491.

World.title: ASX edges higher as Wall Street climbs; Corporate Travel plummets
World.content:
Updated BusinessMarketsWorld markets ASX edges higher as Wall Street climbs; Corporate Travel plummets Staff writers Updated September 3, 2026 — 11:22am ,first published September 3, 2026 — 5:14am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

The Australian sharemarket has inched higher at the open after stocks rose on Wall Street overnight as gains by big technology companies and relatively steady oil prices and bond yields helped boost the market after a downbeat start to the week. The S&P/ASX 200 was up 12.4 points, or 0.1 per cent, in early trade to 8990.8. The ASX lost 1 per cent on Wednesday. The Australian dollar is stronger at US71.71¢. Wall Street climbed as oil prices and bond yields steadied. AP Shares of Corporate Travel Management plunged more than 80 per cent to a low of $2.81 after the recommenced trading, more than a year after the discovery of significant overcharging and accounting errors in its UK/Europe operations. This week the company finally released audited financial statements for the 2025 and 2026 financial years. The 2026 accounts for the year ending June 30 received a qualified opinion from its auditors and reported a net profit of $17.7 million, compared to a loss of $348.5 million in the previous year due to significant writedowns.



Mining stocks are largely stronger, with Fortescue up 2.1 per cent and Rio Tinto 1.3 per cent stronger. BHP was down 2.1 per cent as it traded ex-dividend. Gold miners advanced, with the price of the precious metal holding a gain to trade at about $US4385 an ounce as US President Donald Trump appeared to rule out prolonged military action in the Middle East, easing inflationary concerns of a renewed spike in energy prices. Northern Star and Evolution Mining added 1.6 per cent in early trade. Financial stocks are higher with ANZ Bank leading the way with a 1.1 per cent gain. Commonwealth Bank inched up 0.1 per cent, National Australia Bank added 0.5 per cent and Westpac was 0.6 per cent higher in early trade. Energy stocks slid as oil prices dipped overnight. Brent, the international standard, was down 0.4 per cent in early Asian trade to $US95.26 a barrel. Woodside Energy lost 3 per cent as it traded ex-dividend while Santos slipped 0.3 per cent. Among the refiners, Ampol shed 0.7 per cent and Viva Energy lost 0.5 per cent. Brent crude settled up 1 per cent at $US95.63. Chevron edged 0.3 per cent higher after confirming it would expand operations in Venezuela. Technology stocks slid lower as Xero lost 0.1 per cent, WiseTech fell 1.4 per cent, Technology One lost 1.8 per cent and NEXTDC dropped 0.4 per cent. Life360 was 2.6 per cent higher.



Wall Street has been under pressure this week from rising oil prices and a bond-market sell-off. The rocky start to September follows a mostly positive August during which every major index notched a gain for the month. It remains gripped by anxiety over rising prices, government debt and the impact of global conflicts on the US and the global economy. Overnight on Wall Street, technology and communication services stocks accounted for some of the strongest gains. Computer memory seller Micron Technology gained 2.4 per cent. Chipmaker Nvidia, whose big market value tend to give it more influence over the broader market’s direction, rose 3.2 per cent, lifting the Dow Jones Industrial Average by 0.6 per cent. The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq composite both gained 0.5 per cent. Meta added 2.5 per cent as it released its most powerful artificial intelligence model yet, with its chief AI officer saying its capabilities are edging closer to top competitors. Developers can now access and pay for Muse Spark 1.3, an updated version of its most advanced model, the company said. It will soon roll out the update to users of Meta’s social media platforms, like Instagram and Facebook, as well as Meta AI. “This is our biggest jump so far on model performance,” Meta’s chief AI officer Alexandr Wang said in an interview on Wednesday, pointing to advancements in the model’s coding and agentic capabilities (requiring limited supervision to complete tasks on behalf of human users). Wang said the update put Meta on par with recently released AI models from its rivals OpenAI and Anthropic.



Dell Technologies jumped 15.8 per cent for the biggest gain among S&P 500 stocks after delivering strong second-quarter profits amid accelerating demand for artificial intelligence computing. The company also raised its fiscal year revenue outlook. Palo Alto Networks also reported quarterly results that topped Wall Street’s expectations, citing a strong market for AI cybersecurity, but its shares fell 9.3 per cent. Meanwhile, banks and credit card issuers also helped boost the market. Capital One Financial rose 2.5 per cent and American Express added 1.8 per cent. Markets in Europe fell after markets in Asia closed lower. The big focus this week will be the government’s broader employment report for August, which will be released on Friday. The previous report for July showed that the jobs market stalled, with employers cutting positions.



Related Article Opinion

Oil Trump kidnapped Venezuela’s president. Now he’s hijacking its future Stephen Bartholomeusz Senior business columnist Both inflation and the job market have been key focuses for Wall Street and the Federal Reserve. “Friday’s employment report, and perhaps even more importantly next week’s inflation data, will play a significant role in determining whether policymakers decide to raise rates in September,” said Angelo Kourkafas, senior global strategist, investment strategy at Edward Jones, in a research note. The Fed is trying to balance its task of supporting employment and taming inflation. Wall Street expects the central bank to raise interest rates before the year ends in an effort to cool inflation, which remains well above 3 per cent. The Fed has a stated goal of cooling inflation to 2 per cent. The bond market has been selling off, which is a signal that it expects borrowing costs to rise.



The yield on the 10-year Treasury, which tends to impact mortgage rates, rose to 4.80 per cent from 4.79 per cent late on Tuesday. It has been rising steadily throughout the year and was as low as 4.20 per cent at the beginning of 2026. The yield on the two-year Treasury, which closely tracks expectations for Federal Reserve moves on interest rates, held steady at 4.39 per cent. It is significantly higher for the year, though, and was as low as 3.50 per cent at the beginning of 2026. Investors are also betting on a 64 per cent chance that the Fed will raise rates at its upcoming meeting in September, according to CME FedWatch.
